BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r1.claim: Breaking God’s covenant means opposing and abandoning His command; naqḍ literally means undoing or unfastening a joined structure.

BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r2.claim: Calling covenant-breaking ‘undoing’ is apt because covenant is metaphorically a rope that secures a bond between the parties.
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r2.anchor: من حيث تسميتهم العهد بالحبل على سبيل الاستعارة لما فيه من ثبات الوصلة بين المتعاهدين

BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r3.claim: One account counts three covenants: Adam’s descendants acknowledge God’s lordship, prophets establish religion without division, and scholars disclose rather than conceal truth.
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r3.anchor: قيل : عهد الله ثلاثة : الأول ما أخذه على ذرية آدم عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r4.claim: The pronoun in ‘after its covenant’ may refer to the covenant itself, or to God who confirmed it by sending scriptures and messengers; mīthāq can mean the act of confirmation.
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r4.anchor: فالضمير للعهد أو بعد توثيق الله ذلك بإنزال الكتب وإرسال الرسل فالضمير إلى الله

BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r5.claim: Mālik b. Dīnār recounts a cousin who repeatedly vowed to leave an oppressive sultan’s service when ill, broke each vow after recovery, and died after a final divine rebuke called him a liar.
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r5.anchor: يحكى عن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله أنه كان له ابن عم عامل سلطان في زمانهم وكان ظالما جائرا

BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r6.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r6.claim: The Mathnawī says breaking covenants and vows ultimately brings a curse.
BURSEVI:v1p68#2/r6.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : نقض ميثاق وشكست توبها

BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r1.claim: Grammatically, ‘to be joined’ is an appositive to the relative object; its scope includes every rupture God disapproves: kinship, solidarity among believers, affirming prophets and scriptures together, congregational duties, and abandoning good or doing evil.
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r1.anchor: محل أن يوصل النصب على أنه بدل من ضمير الموصول

BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r2.claim: Such ruptures sever the intended bond between God and servant, which is the purpose underlying every joining and separation.
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r2.anchor: فإنه يقطع ما بين الله تعالى وبين العبد من الوصلة التي هي المقصودة بالذات

BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r3.claim: A report warns that people who display knowledge but neglect it, love with their tongues but hate in their hearts, and sever kinship incur God’s curse and loss of hearing and sight.
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث "إذا أظهر الناس العلم وضيعوا العمل به

BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r4.claim: A report promises divine shade to a widow who raises her young orphans rather than remarrying, a wealthy person who feeds orphans and the poor, and one who maintains kinship; the last receives expanded provision and lifespan.
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r4.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم "ثلاثة في ظل عرش الله يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r5.claim: Corruption in the land consists of blocking faith, mocking truth, and cutting the ties that sustain worldly order and flourishing.
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r5.anchor: بالمنع عن الإيمان والاستهزاء بالحق وقطع الوصل التي عليها يدور فلك نظام العالم وصلاحه

BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r6.claim: The losers trade fidelity for breach, connection for severance, rectitude for corruption, and reward for punishment.
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r6.anchor: لأنهم استبدلوا النقض بالوفاء والقطع بالوصل والفساد بالصلاح وعقابها بثوابها

BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r7.claim: It is said that every person has a home, family, and servants in Paradise; the obedient reaches them, while the disobedient loses them to a believer and is cheated of his share.
BURSEVI:v1p68#3/r7.anchor: قيل : ليس من مؤمن ولا كافر إلا وله منزل وأهل

BURSEVI:v1p69/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p69/r5.claim: The primordial covenant bound people to monotheism and sincere servitude; severing means cutting the paths of spiritual wayfaring to God and retreat from creation.
BURSEVI:v1p69/r5.anchor: يوم الميثاق على التوحيد والعبودية بالإخلاص من بعد ميثاقه

BURSEVI:v1p69/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p69/r6.claim: The paths to be joined are means of spiritual wayfaring and withdrawal from creation toward God.
BURSEVI:v1p69/r6.anchor: من أسباب السلوك الموصل إلى الحق وأسباب التبتل والانقطاع عن الخلق

BURSEVI:v1p69/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p69/r7.claim: They corrupt the innate seed of monotheism by associating partners and rejecting the prophets, failing to water it with faith and righteous deeds; thus they lose human perfection as a seed loses its potential without water.
BURSEVI:v1p69/r7.anchor: يفسدون بذر التوحيد الفطري في أرض طينتهم بالشرك والإعراض عن قبول دعوة الأنبياء

QASHANI:2:27/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:27/r1.claim: The broken covenant is the primordial testimony that God is Lord, linked to the covenant in 7:172 and a report that God brought Adam's descendants out.
QASHANI:2:27/r1.anchor: هو الذي أشار إليه في قوله:

QASHANI:2:27/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:27/r2.claim: An unattributed hadith says God wiped Adam's back with His hand and brought his descendants out like particles; Qashani gives no grading.
QASHANI:2:27/r2.anchor: أن الله تعالى مسح ظهر آدم بيده وأخرج ذريته منه كهيئة الذر

QASHANI:2:27/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:27/r3.claim: Esoterically, God's hand is the holy intellect and first spirit, while Adam is the universal rational soul and heart of the world; the intellect illuminates it and offspring are individual souls actualized from potential.
QASHANI:2:27/r3.anchor: فيد الله هو العقل الأقدس، والروح الأول الذي هو روح العالم المسمى يمين الرحمن

QASHANI:2:27/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:27/r4.claim: The primordial question deposits knowledge of unity and its confirmation plants proofs in the intellect as essential knowledge that appears when veils fall.
QASHANI:2:27/r4.anchor: إيداع علم التوحيد في ذواتهم وميثاق ذلك العهد ركز أدلة التوحيد في عقولهم

QASHANI:2:27/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:27/r5.claim: The answer “Yes” is innate acceptance; breaking the covenant means immersion in bodily pleasures, natural veils, caprice, and desire that obscure unity and worship.
QASHANI:2:27/r5.anchor: قبولهم الذاتي له، ونقض ذلك العهد انهماكهم في اللذات البدنية والغواشي الطبيعية وتعبدهم لهواهم وشهواتهم

QASHANI:2:27/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:27/r6.claim: Severing what God ordered joined means turning from the Holy Spirit, higher principles, celestial spirits, and the inhabitants of divine realms, one's true kin.
QASHANI:2:27/r6.anchor: إعراضهم عن اتصال روح القدس والمبادئ العالية والأرواح السماوية التي هي الملأ الأعلى

QASHANI:2:27/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:2:27/r7.claim: The Prophet is cited as teaching that God loves elevated, noble aims and hates base ones; Qashani gives no grading.
QASHANI:2:27/r7.anchor: إن الله يحب معالي الأمور وأشرافها، ويبغض سفاسفها

QASHANI:2:27#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:27#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:27#2/r1.claim: Corruption on earth and loss mean wasting the lasting luminous substance for something dark and perishable.
QASHANI:2:27#2/r1.anchor: والخسران الذي هو تضييع الجوهر النوري الباقي لأجل الظلماني الفاني.

AKHFASH:v1p60/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p60/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p60/r1.claim: أن يوصل is an appositive to the pronoun in به, like مررت بالقوم بعضهم.
AKHFASH:v1p60/r1.anchor: ف"أن يوصل" بدل من الهاء في "به" كقولك "مررت بالقوم بعضهم"

AKHFASH:v1p60/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p60/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p60/r2.claim: ميثاقه stands for the verbal noun التوثق, like نبات for إنبات and العطاء for الإعطاء.
AKHFASH:v1p60/r2.anchor: وأما "ميثاقه" فصار مكان "التوثق" كما قال {أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا} والاصل "إنباتا"

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#2/r1.claim: God gave them commands, they accepted and pledged to keep them, then broke the covenant by casting it aside and failing to act on it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#2/r1.anchor: أمرهم بأمور فقبلوها عنه، وذلك أخذ الميثاق

NAHHAS:v1p204/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r8.claim: الذين is accusative as an adjective of الفاسقين, or nominative as predicate of an omitted subject, هم.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r8.anchor: الذين في موضع نصب على النعت للفاسقين وإن شئت جعلته في موضع رفع

NAHHAS:v1p204/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r9.claim: ينقضون is imperfect, with its implicit subject referring back to الذين; عهد الله is its object.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r9.anchor: ينقضون ) فعل مستقبل والمضمر الذي فيه يعود على الذين ( عهد الله ) مفعول به

NAHHAS:v1p204/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r10.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v1p204/r10.claim: Ibn Kaysan says ميثاق is a noun standing in for a verbal noun, meaning إيثاق.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r10.anchor: قال ابن كيسان هو اسم يؤدي عن المصدر

NAHHAS:v1p204/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r11.speaker: القطامي
NAHHAS:v1p204/r11.claim: Al-Qutami’s verse is cited as usage evidence with بعد and the verbal noun عطائك.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r11.anchor: قال القطامي ( أكفرا بعد رد الموت عني … وبعد عطائك المائة الرتاعا

NAHHAS:v1p204/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r12.claim: ويقطعون is coordinated with ينقضون; ما أمر الله به is its accusative object.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r12.anchor: ويقطعون ) عطف على ينقصون ( ما أمر الله به ) ما في موضع نصب بيقطعون

NAHHAS:v1p204/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r13.claim: The root ق ط ع has several forms and senses: severing, crossing a river, migrating birds, scarce water, and breathlessness.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r13.anchor: وقطعت الحبل قطعا وقطعت النهر قطوعا وقطعت الطير قطاعا

NAHHAS:v1p204/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r14.claim: يفسدون is coordinated with يقطعون; أولئك begins a sentence and هم with الخاسرون forms its predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r14.anchor: ويفسدون في الأرض ) عطف على يقطعون ( أولئك ) مبتدأ ( هم ) ابتداء ثان

NAHHAS:v1p204/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r15.claim: Alternatively, هم is extra and الخاسرون alone is the predicate of أولئك.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r15.anchor: إن شئت كانت هم زائدة والخاسرون الخبر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r1.speaker: سعد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r1.claim: Saʿd identified the covenant breakers in this verse as the Haruriyya (Kharijites).
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r1.anchor: عن مصعب بن سعد قال : سالت أبي فقلت : قوله : الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه إلى اخر الاية . فقال : هم الحرورية

IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r2.claim: The verse lists six hypocritical traits when they have power: lying, breaking promises, betraying trusts, breaking God’s covenant, severing commanded ties, and corruption; when weak, they show only the first three.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه إلى قوله : اولئك هم الخاسرون قال هي ست خصال في المنافقين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r3.claim: The covenant is the primordial pledge to worship God and associate no partners with Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان : قول الله : الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه يعني ميثاقه الاول الذي اخذ عليهم ان يعبدوه ولا يشركوا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r4.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r4.claim: The covenant was the one made with them in the Qur’an: they acknowledged it, then disbelieved and broke it.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r4.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه هو ماعهد اليهم في القران ، فاقروا به ، ثم كفروا فنقضوه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r5.claim: The Torah covenant required them to believe and affirm Muhammad; they disbelieved and broke that covenant as well as the first one.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r5.anchor: عن مقاتل ابن حيان : قوله : من بعد ميثاقه في التوراة ان يؤمنوا بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ويصدقوه ، فكفروا ونقضوا الميثاق الاول

IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r6.speaker: سعد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r6.claim: Saʿd also applied the description of those who sever what God commanded to the Haruriyya.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p71/r6.anchor: عن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال : الحرورية الذين قال الله : ويعطون ما امر الله به ان يوصل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r1.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r1.claim: What God commanded to be joined includes kinship ties.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r1.anchor: عن السدى : ويقطعون ما امر الله به ان يوصل من الارحام

IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r2.claim: It also means believing in Muhammad and all earlier prophets and messengers without distinguishing among them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : ويقطعون ما امر الله به ان يوصل في محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والنبيين والمرسلين من قبله ، ان يؤمنوا جميعا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r3.speaker: سعد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r3.claim: Saʿd explained their corruption in the land by calling them evildoers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r3.anchor: عن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه : ويفسدون في الأرض فكان سعد يسميهم الفاسقين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r4.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r4.claim: Corruption in the land means committing acts of disobedience there.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r4.anchor: عن السدى : ويفسدون في الأرض يعملون فيها بالمعصية

IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r5.claim: Corruption means their evil deeds committed on earth.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r5.anchor: عن مقاتل في قوله : ويفسدون في الأرض قال اعمالهم السيئة التي يعملون بها في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r6.claim: The losers are the people of the Fire in the Hereafter.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p72/r6.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان : قوله اولئك هم الخاسرون في الاخرة . يقول : هم اهل النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p366#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p366#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p366#2/r4.claim: The covenant-breaking relative clause describes the fasiqin; parsing it as a detached subject with 2:27's ending as predicate changes syntax but not the coherent characterization, so the descriptive parse is stronger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p366#2/r4.anchor: إلى آخره صفة للفاسقين لتقرير اتصافهم بالفسق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r1.claim: Breaking a covenant is pictured as gradually and repeatedly untying a cord; naqḍ conveys destruction more forcefully than cutting or severing, which merely divides.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r1.anchor: ووجه اختيار استعارة النقض الذي هو حل طيات الحبل إلى إبطال العهد أنها تمثيل لإبطال العهد رويدا رويدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r2.claim: The phrase combines an implicit cord metaphor with an explicit representational metaphor; the accompanying word naqḍ evokes the absent cord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r2.anchor: وفي النقض رمز إلى استعارة مكنية لأن النقض من روادف الحبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r3.claim: Abu Firas's claws and fangs for warriors and Labid's hand of the north wind illustrate a metaphor's associated feature used as imaginative fiction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r4.claim: The author also cites an unattributed verse about severed ties and another urging the cutting of a strained attachment as poetic parallels for breaking bonds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r4.anchor: فاقطع لبانة من تعرض وصله فلشر واصل خلة صرامها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r5.claim: A metaphorical feature may stand alone, link to an implicit metaphor as here, or reinforce an explicit metaphor; these classifications can overlap and depend on the rhetorician's focus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p368/r5.anchor: وإنما التقسيم بالنظر إلى ما ينظر إليه البليغ أول النظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r1.claim: Naqḍ is undoing something firmly tied so it returns to its original unbound state; ʿahd here is a prior commitment or injunction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r1.anchor: النقض رد ما أبرم على أوله غير مبرم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r2.claim: One interpretation identifies the covenant as God's primordial covenant with Adam's descendants, drawn out like particles from his back.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r2.anchor: أخذه الله على بني آدم حين استخرجهم من ظهر أبيهم آدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation calls the signs of God's oneness in the heavens, earth, and created order themselves a covenant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r3.anchor: نصب الأدلة على وحدانية الله بالسماوات والأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r4.claim: A further view makes the covenant transmitted through messengers: worship God alone and worship no other.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r4.anchor: بواسطة رسله أن يوحدوه وأن لا يعبدوا غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r5.claim: Others identify the covenant of scriptural communities as belief in Muḥammad and not concealing his status; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this specifically concerns the People of the Book, though surrounding context concerns all disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r5.anchor: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأن لا يكتموا أمره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r6.claim: Qatāda says the verse is about people who believed in the Prophet and then disbelieved, thereby breaking their covenant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r6.anchor: هذه الآية هي فيمن كان آمن بالنبي عليه السلام ثم كفر به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī did not attribute these interpretations; any covenant made lawfully among Muslims may not be broken under this verse. The pronoun in mīthāqihi can refer to the covenant or to God's name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r7.anchor: وكل عهد جائز بين المسلمين فنقضه لا يحل بهذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r8.claim: Mīthāq is a noun for the act of binding, from wathāqa; the verse uses it as a verbal noun, as in ʿAmr b. Shayyim's line meaning “after your giving.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r8.anchor: وهو في هذه الآية اسم في موضع المصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r9.claim: Qatāda understands the thing severed as kinship generally among people; another view narrows it to kinship between believers and says disbelievers severed ties with those who followed Muḥammad.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r10.speaker: جمهور أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r10.claim: Most scholars say the connection to be maintained is God's religion and worship on earth, observance of its laws, and preservation of its limits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p112#2/r10.anchor: الإشارة في هذه الآية إلى دين الله وعبادته في الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r1.claim: He endorses the majority interpretation of maintaining God's religion and says kinship is one part of it; the clause with an is accusative as an appositive to mā or as purpose, with a genitive appositional analysis also possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r1.anchor: وهذا هو الحق، والرحم جزء من هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r2.claim: Corruption on earth means worshiping other than God and acting unjustly according to desires; loss is depriving oneself of a share in success and triumph.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r2.anchor: يفسدون في الأرض يعبدون غير الله ويجورون في الأفعال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r1.claim: “Those who break” describes the previously discussed three kinds of transgressors; naqd is the opposite of binding, undoing something after it is secured.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r1.anchor: هذه صفة للفاسقين وقد سبقت فيهم الأقوال الثلاثة والنقض ضد الإبرام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r2.claim: Breaking a structure means dismantling what was firmly assembled; breaking a covenant means refusing to abide by its terms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r2.anchor: فنقض البناء تفريق جمعه بعد إحكامه ونقض العهد الإعراض عن المقام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil say the covenant with the People of the Book concerned Muhammad’s description and the command to follow him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r3.anchor: أنه ما عهد إلى أهل الكتاب من صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والوصية باتباعه قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says it was the covenant they accepted in the Qur’an and then repudiated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r4.anchor: ما عهد إليهم في القرآن فأقروا به ثم كفروا قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies it as the covenant taken from Adam’s descendants; although unmentioned earlier, the author says a truthful report establishes it and requires belief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r5.anchor: الذي أخذه عليهم حين استخرج ذرية آدم من ظهره قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r6.claim: The particle min in “after its covenant” is either extra or marks a starting point: the breaking began after the covenant was firmly made.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r6.anchor: أنها زائدة والثاني أنها لابتداء الغاية كأنه قال ابتداء نقض العهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r7.claim: The pronoun in “its covenant” may refer to God or to the covenant, meaning after its firm establishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r7.anchor: أنها ترجع إلى الله تعالى والثاني أنها ترجع إلى العهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and al-Suddi say what God commanded to be joined is kinship and family ties.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r8.anchor: الرحم والقرابة قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the command was to maintain connection with the Messenger, which they severed by denying him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r9.anchor: أنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قطعوه بالتكذيب قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r10.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r10.claim: Muqatil says it is faith in God without dividing among His messengers; they believed in some and disbelieved in others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r10.anchor: الإيمان بالله وأن لا يفرق بين أحد من رسله فآمنوا ببعض وكفروا بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says their corruption on earth was calling people to unbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r11.anchor: استدعاؤهم الناس إلى الكفر قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r12.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r12.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil explain the corruption as committing sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r12.anchor: أنه العمل بالمعاصي قاله السدي و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r13.claim: A third explanation is their intercepting people migrating to the Prophet to prevent conversion to Islam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r13.anchor: أنه قطعهم الطريق على من جاء مهاجرا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليمنعوا الناس من الاسلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p56/r14.claim: Khusrān means loss or diminution in Arabic.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p206#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p206#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p206#2/r1.claim: When the hypocrites heard the fire and rainstorm parables, they objected that God was too exalted to use such examples; this occasioned the passage through 'the losers.'
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p206#2/r1.anchor: قال المنافقون: الله أعلى وأجل من أن يضرب هذه الأمثال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r5.claim: In another report, Sa'd identifies those who break God's covenant as the Haruriyya; Ibn Kathir says this is an interpretation if the report is sound, not a claim that the verse specifically predicts the Khawarij.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r5.anchor: فقال: هم الحرورية. وهذا الإسناد إن صح عن سعد بن أبي وقاص، رضي الله عنه، فهو تفسير على المعنى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r6.claim: The Haruriyya arose after revelation, but they fall under the verse's description because they left the imam's obedience and Islamic ordinances.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r6.anchor: فإن أولئك لم يكونوا حال نزول الآية، وإنما هم داخلون بوصفهم فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r7.claim: In Arabic, فسق means leaving obedience; the date leaves its skin and a mouse is called a little fasiq for leaving its hole to cause harm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r7.anchor: والفاسق في اللغة: هو الخارج عن الطاعة أيضا. وتقول العرب: فسقت الرطبة:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r8.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r8.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections permits killing five harmful creatures in the sanctuary and outside it: crow, kite, scorpion, mouse, and vicious dog.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r8.anchor: خمس فواسق يقتلن في الحل والحرم: الغراب، والحدأة، والعقرب، والفأرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r9.claim: Fasq includes both unbelief and sin, but the unbeliever's is graver; the intended fasiqun here are unbelievers, as the following traits distinguish them from believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p209/r9.anchor: فالفاسق يشمل (1) الكافر والعاصي، ولكن فسق الكافر أشد وأفحش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r1.claim: One view takes the covenant as God's commands to obey and prohibitions against disobedience, conveyed in scripture and through messengers; breaking it means failing to act on it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r1.anchor: هو وصية الله إلى خلقه وأمره إياهم بما أمرهم به من طاعته، ونهيه إياهم عما نهاهم عنه من معصيته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r2.speaker: ابن جرير ومقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r2.claim: They identify the covenant with the Torah's charge to its People of the Book to follow Muhammad when sent and affirm him; breaking it is knowingly denying him and concealing what they had pledged to disclose.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r2.anchor: وهذا اختيار ابن جرير رحمه الله وقول مقاتل بن حيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r3.claim: Another view extends the verse to all unbelievers, polytheists, and hypocrites: God gave them rational evidence of His lordship and prophetic miracles, yet they denied the truth of messengers and scriptures.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r3.anchor: بل عنى بهذه الآية جميع أهل الكفر والشرك والنفاق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this broad interpretation good; al-Zamakhshari leans toward it, taking the covenant as the rational evidence for God's oneness, like the primordial testimony and the covenant in scripture.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r5.claim: A further view identifies the covenant as the pledge God took from Adam's descendants; breaking it means failing to fulfill it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p210/r5.anchor: العهد الذي أخذه عليهم حين أخرجهم من صلب آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r1.claim: Hypocrites show six traits when they have the upper hand: lying, breaking promises, betraying trusts, breaking God's covenant, severing commanded ties, and spreading corruption; when weak they show only the first three. Rabi ibn Anas agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r1.anchor: قال: هي ست خصال من (3) المنافقين إذا كانت فيهم الظهرة (4) على الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r2.claim: The covenant was the Qur'an's charge, which people accepted and then broke by disbelieving.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211/r2.anchor: هو ما عهد إليهم في القرآن فأقروا به ثم كفروا فنقضوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.speaker: قتادة وابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.claim: The severed connection means kinship ties, as in 47:22; Ibn Jarir favors this interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.anchor: قيل: المراد به صلة الأرحام والقرابات، كما فسره قتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.claim: A broader interpretation includes everything God commanded people to connect or do, which they severed or abandoned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.anchor: فكل ما أمر الله بوصله وفعله قطعوه وتركوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.claim: He says these losers lose in the afterlife, as also stated in 13:25.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.anchor: قال (8) في الآخرة، وهذا كما قال تعالى: {أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.claim: As transmitted by al-Dahhak, loss attributed to non-Muslims means unbelief, while loss attributed to Muslims means sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.anchor: كل شيء نسبه الله إلى غير أهل الإسلام من اسم مثل خاسر، فإنما يعني به الكفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.claim: Losers are those who diminish their own selves and share of God's mercy through disobedience, like a merchant who loses capital; disbelievers and hypocrites are deprived of mercy when most in need of it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.anchor: الخاسرون: جمع خاسر، وهم الناقصون أنفسهم [و] (9) حظوظهم بمعصيتهم الله من رحمته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.speaker: جرير بن عطية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari cites Jarir's verse as lexical evidence for خسار, the verbal noun meaning loss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.anchor: إن سليطا في الخسار إنه … أولاد قوم خلقوا أقنه

JISHUMI:v1p299/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p299/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p299/r7.claim: Breaking undoes what was firmly joined, opposite to binding or sound construction; metaphorically it invalidates a doctrine or proof.
JISHUMI:v1p299/r7.anchor: النقض والهدم والكسر نظائر، وهو إفساد ما أبرمت، ونقيضه الإبرام

JISHUMI:v1p299/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p299/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p299/r8.claim: Covenant can mean a command, testament, or binding pact; covenant, compact, and bond share the sense of firmness.
JISHUMI:v1p299/r8.anchor: والعهد: الأمر، والعهد: الوصية، والعهد: الموثق، والجمع: عهود

JISHUMI:v1p299/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p299/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p299/r9.claim: Every morally responsible person receives God's covenant through rational proofs of the Creator and Benefactor and through commands and prohibitions delivered by messengers.
JISHUMI:v1p299/r9.anchor: وكل مكلف فقد أخذ الله عليه الميثاق بشيئين: بما ركب في عقله

JISHUMI:v1p299/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p299/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p299/r10.claim: Cutting is the opposite of joining; the doubled form can indicate repeated or emphatic cutting, while joining means combining or attaching.

JISHUMI:v1p300/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p300/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p300/r1.claim: Commands may express obligation, recommendation, permission, threat, challenge, or creation; their basic meaning is a request, and most scholars say they imply obligation.
JISHUMI:v1p300/r1.anchor: والأصل في الجميع الطلب، وحقيقة الأمر في القول

JISHUMI:v1p300/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p300/r2.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v1p300/r2.claim: They hold that commands indicate recommendation, unlike the majority view of obligation; the author rejects suspending judgment as untenable.
JISHUMI:v1p300/r2.anchor: وقيل: على الندب، عن أبي علي وأبي هاشم، وقيل: على التوقف، وليس بشيء.

JISHUMI:v1p300/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p300/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p300/r3.claim: Loss is the opposite of profit and fundamentally means losing one's capital.

JISHUMI:v1p300/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p300/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p300/r4.claim: الذين is accusative as an adjective qualifying the sinful, or nominative as a condemnatory clause whose predicate is ‘those are the losers.’
JISHUMI:v1p300/r4.anchor: نصب؛ لأنه صفة للفاسقين، ويصلح الرفع على الذم

JISHUMI:v1p300/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p300/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p300/r5.claim: من after ‘after’ may be an extra particle or mark the starting point of breaking; أن يوصل may be genitive as a substitute or accusative as an object.
JISHUMI:v1p300/r5.anchor: قيل: صلة وزيادة، وقيل: معناها ابتداء الغاية

JISHUMI:v1p300/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p300/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p300/r6.claim: God's covenant may be rational evidence, the prophetic promise concerning Muhammad recorded in earlier scriptures, or God's commands and prohibitions; the latter is reported from Abu Muslim.
JISHUMI:v1p300/r6.anchor: وقيل: ما قدم إليهم على ألسن الرسل من صفة محمد

JISHUMI:v1p300/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p300/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p300/r7.claim: The claim that this is the covenant taken from Adam's descendants is rejected because people do not remember it and there is no evidence, so it cannot establish an obligation.
JISHUMI:v1p300/r7.anchor: فأما من قال: إنه العهد الذي أخذه الله تعالى على ذرية آدم

JISHUMI:v1p301/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p301/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p301/r1.claim: The people described may be Jewish scholars, including hypocrites, or all unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v1p301/r1.anchor: قيل: أحبار اليهود، ومنهم المنافقون، وقيل: جميع الكفار.

JISHUMI:v1p301/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p301/r2.claim: The pronoun in ‘after its covenant’ may refer to God, who confirmed it, or to the covenant itself; both readings are acceptable.
JISHUMI:v1p301/r2.anchor: قيل: تعود على اسم الله تعالى، يعني أنه وكده عليهم، وقيل: ترجع على الميثاق

JISHUMI:v1p301/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p301/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p301/r3.claim: Breaking what God ordered joined may mean severing kinship with the Messenger from enmity and envy; reports also mention the Prophet and believers, kinship ties, or belief in all prophets and scriptures, and the author allows the broad sense to cover all.
JISHUMI:v1p301/r3.anchor: وقيل: قطعوا رحم رسول الله بعداوته بغضا وحسدا، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v1p301/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p301/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p301/r4.claim: Corruption means inviting others to disbelief, practicing disbelief, or resulting insecurity, banditry, and injustice that faith would prevent.
JISHUMI:v1p301/r4.anchor: قيل: استدعاؤهم إلى الكفر هو الفساد، وقيل: عملهم به

JISHUMI:v1p301/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p301/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p301/r5.claim: Losers have ruined themselves like those who lose their capital; alternatively they miss Paradise and deserve the Fire.
JISHUMI:v1p301/r5.anchor: أولئك هم الخاسرون أي أهلكوا أنفسهم فهم بمنزلة من هلك رأس ماله

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r1.claim: الذين ينقضون may be an adjective of الفاسقين, an accusative of censure, a subject whose predicate is أولئك هم الخاسرون, or predicate of an omitted هم الفاسقون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r1.anchor: فيه أربعة أوجه، أحدها: أن يكون نعتا للفاسقين.

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r2.claim: نقض means undoing an assembled thing back to its prior state; عهد can mean testament, guarantee, entrustment, or command.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r2.anchor: والنقض: حل تركيب الشيء والرجوع به إلى الحالة الأولى.

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r3.speaker: جرير
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r3.claim: Jarir's line uses الخسار for loss or deficiency; خسرت and أخسرته mean to reduce something, while خسران، خسار، خيسرى mean ruin.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r3.anchor:
قال جرير:
316 إن سليطا في الخسار إنه

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r4.claim: من بعد attaches to ينقضون and من marks starting point; the alternative that من is extra is rejected.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r4.anchor: و " من بعد " متعلق ب " ينقضون " ، و " من " لابتداء الغاية

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r5.claim: The pronoun in ميثاقه can refer to عهد, making the verbal noun object-related, or to Allah, making it subject-related; ميثاق means birth or promise.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r5.anchor: فهو على الأول مصدر مضاف إلى المفعول، وعلى الثاني مضاف للفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats ميثاق as a noun in place of a verbal noun, citing عطائك for إعطائك; the author sees no need for this analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " وهو اسم في موضع المصدر كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r7.claim: The root carries the sense of binding; its plurals are مواثيق and مياثق, with Ibn al-A'rabi's verse witnessing عهد المياثق.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r7.anchor: والمادة تدل على الشد والربط وجمعه مواثيق ومياثق

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r8.claim: ويقطعون is coordinated with ينقضون as another relative-clause verb; ما is relative and its clause is أمر الله به, while Abu al-Baqa allows an indefinite described ما.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r8.anchor: عطف على " ينقصون " فهي صلة أيضا، و " ما " موصولة

SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r9.speaker: أبو الحسن وابن السراج
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r9.claim: Only Abu al-Hasan and Ibn al-Sarraj allow ما to be a verbal noun here despite the returning pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27/r9.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تكون مصدرية لعود الضمير عليها إلا عند أبي الحسن وابن السراج

SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r1.claim: أن يوصل may be genitive apposition to the pronoun in به, as in Imruʾ al-Qays; it may be an accusative appositive to ما, or a purpose object estimated as كراهة أن يوصل or أن لا يوصل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r1.anchor: الجر على البدل من الضمير في " به " أي: ما أمر الله بوصله،

SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows أن يوصل as the predicate of an omitted subject هو, a very remote analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r2.anchor: والرفع [على] أنه خبر مبتدأ مضمر أي هو أن يوصل

SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r3.claim: يفسدون is coordinated with the relative-clause verbs, and في الأرض attaches to it; the الخاسرون clause echoes the phrasing of 2:5.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r3.anchor: و { يفسدون } عطف على الصلة أيضا و { في الأرض } متعلق به

SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r4.claim: أولئك هم الخاسرون is a predicate if الذين is a subject; otherwise it is a fresh sentence without syntactic position. خسر means loss, and الأمر is a superior's request to an inferior.
SAMIN-DURR:2:27#2/r4.anchor: وتقدم معنى الخسار، والأمر: طلب الأعلى من الأدنى.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r10.claim: Naqḍ is the opposite of binding firmly; ʿahd may mean a testament or a binding covenant, and mīthāq is what makes a pledge secure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r10.anchor: أما النقض , فهو ضد الإبرام , وفي العهد قولان : أحدهما : الوصية . والثاني : الموثق . والميثاق ما وقع التوثق به

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r11.claim: God's covenant may be His commands in scripture and through messengers to obey and avoid sin; breaking it is failure to act on them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r11.anchor: وصية الله إلى خلقه وأمره إياهم بما أمرهم به من طاعة , ونهيه إياهم عما نهاهم عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r12.claim: The covenant may be the rational proof God created in people for His oneness and the truth of messengers, confirmed by miracles.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r12.anchor: ما خلقه في عقولهم من الحجة على توحيده وصدق رسله بالمعجزات

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r13.claim: It may be scripture's description of the Prophet and command to follow him, which the People of the Book denied after pledging to disclose it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r13.anchor: ما أنزله على أهل الكتاب [ من ] , على صفة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , والوصية المؤكدة باتباعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r14.claim: It may be the covenant taken from Adam's descendants, described in the cited verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r14.anchor: العهد الذي أخذه عليهم حين أخرجهم من صلب آدم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r15.claim: The pronoun in “after its covenant” may refer to God, or to the covenant itself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r15.anchor: كناية ترجع إلى اسم الله وتقديره من بعد ميثاق الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r16.claim: The address may target hypocrites, the People of the Book, or all disbelievers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r16.anchor: وفيمن عناه الله تعالى بهذا الخطاب , ثلاثة أقاويل : أحدها : المنافقون . والثاني : أهل الكتاب . والثالث : جميع الكفار

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r17.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r17.claim: What God commands to be joined is His Messenger, whom they sever through denial and disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r17.anchor: هو رسوله , فقطعوه بالتكذيب والعصيان , وهو قول الحسن البصري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r18.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r18.claim: What God commands to be joined is kinship and family ties.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r18.anchor: والثاني : أنه الرحم والقرابة , وهو قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r19.claim: The phrase may broadly cover everything God commands people to join.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r19.anchor: والثالث : أنه على العموم في كل ما أمر الله تعالى به أن يوصل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r20.claim: Corruption on earth may mean inviting others to disbelief.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r21.claim: Corruption may mean terrifying travelers and cutting off roads.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r21.anchor: والثاني : أنه إخافتهم السبل وقطعهم الطريق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r22.claim: The losers may be those whose share and honor have diminished; a line by Jarīr uses خسار for loss.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p88/r22.anchor: أحدهما : أن الخسران هو النقصان , ومنه قول جرير

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r1.claim: Alternatively, the losers are those destroyed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r1.anchor: أن الخسران ها هنا الهلاك , ومعناه : أولئك هم الهالكون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r2.claim: When loss is attributed to non-Muslims it means unbelief; when attributed to Muslims it means sin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90/r2.anchor: كل ما نسبه الله تعالى من الخسران إلى غير المسلمين فإنما يعني الكفر

MUQATIL:2:26-27/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:26-27/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:26-27/r4.claim: The Jews broke the Torah covenant to worship God alone and believe in Muhammad, rejected Jesus and Muhammad, and accepted some prophets while rejecting others.
MUQATIL:2:26-27/r4.anchor: فنقضوا العهد الأول، ونقضوا ما أخذ عليهم فى التوراة

MUQATIL:2:26-27/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:26-27/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:26-27/r5.claim: Cutting what God commanded to join means rejecting belief in Muhammad; corruption is acting sinfully, and their loss is punishment, as paralleled in 13:25.
MUQATIL:2:26-27/r5.anchor: ونظيرها فى الرعد: { الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r1.claim: The breakers of God's covenant may be obstinate Jewish scholars, their hypocrites, or disbelievers generally.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r1.anchor: والمراد بهؤلاء الناقضين لعهد الله احبار اليهود المتعنتون أو منافقوهم أو الكفار جميعا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r2.claim: The covenant may be the rational evidence for God's oneness implanted in human minds, treated as a binding charge.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r2.anchor: ما ركز فى عقولهم من الحجة على التوحيد كأنه أمر وصاهم به ووثقه عليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r3.claim: It may be the pledge to affirm and follow a messenger whom God supports with miracles, rather than conceal his description.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r3.anchor: بأنهم إذا بعث إليهم رسول يصدقه الله بمعجزاته صدقوه واتبعوه ولم يكتموا ذكره

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r4.claim: Another interpretation is a pledge not to shed one another's blood, oppress one another, or sever kinship.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r4.anchor: أن لا يسفكوا دماءهم ولا يبغى بعضهم على بعض ولا يقطعوا أرحامهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r5.claim: A threefold account distinguishes the primordial covenant with Adam's descendants, the prophets' duty to convey revelation, and scholars' duty to disclose scripture.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r5.anchor: عهد الله إلى خلقه ثلاثة عهود العهد الأول الذي أخذه على جميع ذرية آدم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r6.claim: Mīthāq derives from firmness; its pronoun refers to the covenant they undertook to keep, or describes God's binding it upon them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r6.anchor: أصله من الوثاقة وهى إحكام الشئ والضمير للعهد وهو ما وثقوا به عهد الله من قبوله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r7.claim: What they sever means either kinship and alliance with believers or the connection among prophets who agree on truth, which they break by selective belief.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r7.anchor: هو قطعهم الأرحام وموالاة المؤمنين أو قطعهم ما بين الانيباء من الوصلة والاجتماع على الحق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r8.claim: The phrase about what God ordered joined has grammatical alternatives: ما is indefinite described by the following clause or a relative pronoun, with أن nominally attached in two ways.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r8.anchor: وما نكرة موصوفة أو بمعنى الذى و أن يوصل فى موضع جر بدل من الهاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r9.claim: Corruption in the land includes blocking roads and obstructing faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r10.claim: They are the losers: the emphatic pronoun separates the subject, and they are deceived and deprived.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p34/r10.anchor: ﴿ أولئك ﴾ مبتدأ ﴿ هم ﴾ فصل والخبر ﴿ الخاسرون ﴾ أى المغبونون حيث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35/r1.claim: Their loss is exchanging breach for fidelity, severance for connection, corruption for reform, and punishment for reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35/r1.anchor: استبدلوا النقض بالوفاء والقطع بالوصل والفساد بالصلاح والعقاب بالثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r1.claim: الذين may be accusative as an adjective for الفاسقين, or nominative as the predicate of an omitted هو.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r1.anchor: «الذين» في موضع نصب على النعت للفاسقين، وإن شئت جعلته في موضع رفع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r2.claim: نقض is undoing what one has firmly bound, such as a structure, rope, or covenant; the passage also notes related forms for unraveling, contradiction, and counter-poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r2.anchor: النقض: إفساد ما أبرمته من بناء أو حبل أو عهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r3.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r3.claim: One view identifies the covenant as the pledge God took from Adam's descendants when He brought them from his back.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r3.anchor: فقيل: هو الذي أخذه الله على بني آدم حين استخرجهم من ظهره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r4.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r4.claim: Another view makes the covenant God's commands and prohibitions delivered through His books and messengers; breaking it means failing to act on them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو وصية الله تعالى إلى خلقه، وأمره إياهم بما أمرهم به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r5.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r5.claim: Another view treats the signs of God's oneness in the heavens, earth, and creation as a covenant, broken by neglecting to reflect on them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r5.anchor: بل نصب الأدلة على وحدانيته بالسموات والأرض وسائر الصنعة هو بمنزلة العهد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r6.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r6.claim: Another view concerns scriptural communities commanded to disclose Muhammad's prophethood rather than conceal it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r6.anchor: هو ما عهده إلى من أوتي الكتاب أن يبينوا نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يكتموا أمره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r7.claim: He says the covenant God took from prophets and their followers was not to disbelieve in the Prophet, citing the covenant passage in Āl ʿImrān.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: عهده جل وعز ما أخذه على النبيين ومن اتبعهم ألا يكفروا بالنبي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r8.claim: Although the preceding and following context appears to concern unbelievers, he says the second, general account of God's commands gathers the other views.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r8.anchor: قلت: وظاهر ما قبل وما بعد يدل على أنها في الكفار. فهذه خمسة أقوال والقول الثاني يجمعها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r9.claim: ميثاق is a strongly confirmed covenant, from الوثاقة and the firmness of binding; its plurals include مواثيق and dialectal variants, supported by a line cited from Ibn al-Aʿrābī.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r9.anchor: الميثاق: العهد المؤكد باليمين مفعال من الوثاقة والمعاهدة،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r10.claim: The verb يقطعون has several lexical uses: severing kin, cutting a rope, crossing a river, migrating birds, dwindling water, and breathlessness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r10.anchor: القطع معروف، والمصدر في الرحم القطيعة يقال: قطع رحمه قطيعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r11.claim: ما is the object of يقطعون; أن can substitute for ما or its pronoun in به, preferably the pronoun, and may also express aversion to connection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r11.anchor: «ما» في موضع نصب ب «يقطعون». و «أن» إن شئت كانت بدلا من «ما» وإن شئت من الهاء في «به»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r12.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r12.claim: One view says what must be joined is kinship ties.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r12.anchor: واختلف ما الشيء الذي أمر بوصله؟ فقيل: صلة الأرحام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r13.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r13.claim: Another view says they sever profession from practice by speaking without acting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27/r13.anchor: وقيل: أمر أن يوصل القول بالعمل فقطعوا بينهما بأن قالوا ولم يعملوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.claim: Another view says they affirm some prophets but reject others, breaking the command to believe in all of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.anchor: أمرأن يوصل التصديق بجيمع أنبيائه، فقطعوه بتصديق بعضهم وتكذيب بعضهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.claim: The command is general: it includes God's religion, worship, laws, and limits, with kinship one part of what must be joined.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.anchor: فهي عامة في كل ما أمر الله تعالى به أن يوصل. هذا قول الجمهور والرحم جزء من هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.claim: فساد on earth means worshipping other than God and acting unjustly according to desires, the fullest form of corruption.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.anchor: أي يعبدون غير الله تعالى ويجورون في الأفعال، إذ هي بحسب شهواتهم وهذا غاية الفساد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.claim: In أولئك هم الخاسرون, هم may be redundant or may begin a second nominal clause whose predicate completes the first.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.anchor: و «هم» زائدة ويجوز أن تكون «هم» ابتداء ثان، «الخاسرون» خبره،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r5.claim: A loser is one who diminishes his own share of success; خسْران means loss, as illustrated by Jarir's verse about lost share and honor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r5.anchor: والخاسر: الذي نقص نفسه حظها من الفلاح والفوز. والخسران: النقصان،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r6.claim: Al-Jawhari gives خسار, خسارة, and خيسرى senses of misguidance and destruction; the doomed lose themselves and family on Judgment Day and are denied Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r6.anchor: والخسار والخسارة والخيسرى: الضلال والهلاك. فقيل للهالك: خاسر لأنه خسر نفسه وأهله يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r7.claim: The verse establishes that every lawful covenant a person undertakes must be honored, whether made with a Muslim or another person.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r7.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على أن الوفاء بالعهد والتزامه وكل عهد جائز ألزمه المرء نفسه فلا يحل له نقضه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r8.claim: God also commands that a feared betrayal be openly repudiated to the other party, thereby forbidding treachery rather than secret breach.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:27#2/r8.anchor:
وقد قال لنبيه عليه السلام:
وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة فانبذ إليهم على سوآء
[الأنفال: 58] فنهاه عن الغدر،

RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r1.claim: One interpretation is breaking kinship ties and relatives’ rights; it may specifically allude to severing the family relationship with the Prophet, but that makes the verse particular.
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن المراد بهذا الميثاق حججه القائمة على عباده الدالة لهم على صحة توحيده

RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r2.claim: A second interpretation identifies the covenant as a vow by some people to follow a warner if one came; their refusal would breach it, but this applies only to those who swore.
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r2.anchor: وثانيها : يحتمل أن يعني به ما دل عليه بقوله : { وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r3.claim: He prefers the first, general reading because it avoids restricting the verse and grounds blame in rejecting God’s repeatedly established proofs in creation, reason, scripture, and prophecy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r3.anchor: رجحان التأويل الأول على الثاني من وجهين : الأول : أن على التقدير الأول يمكن إجراء الآية

RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r4.claim: Qaffal suggests the verse concerns People of the Book who broke scriptural pledges to affirm Muhammad, his message, and his community.
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r4.anchor: وثالثها : قال القفال : يحتمل أن يكون المقصود بالآية قوما من أهل الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r5.claim: Some identify the covenant with humanity’s primordial pledge; theologians reject this because people cannot fairly be blamed for a pact they do not remember.
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r5.anchor: ورابعا : قال بعضهم ، إنه عنى به ميثاقا أخذه من الناس وهم على صورة الذر

RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r6.claim: A further account distinguishes three covenants: Adam’s descendants acknowledge God’s lordship, prophets promise to convey revelation and uphold one religion, and scholars promise to clarify scripture rather than conceal it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r6.anchor: وخامسها : عهد الله إلى خلقه ثلاثة عهود

RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says “His covenant” can refer to the covenant they accepted, its ratification, or God, who reinforced it through signs, books, and messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p136/r7.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الضمير في ميثاقه للعهد وهو ما وثقوا به عهد الله من قبوله

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r1.claim: One interpretation is severing kinship and relatives’ rights, possibly alluding specifically to cutting family ties with the Prophet; this makes the verse particular.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r1.anchor: أحدها : أراد به قطيعة الرحم وحقوق القرابات التي أمر الله بوصلها

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r2.claim: A second interpretation is severing ties with believers while joining oneself to unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r2.anchor: وثانيها : أن الله تعالى أمرهم أن يصلوا حبلهم بحبل المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r3.claim: A third interpretation is the dissent and strife they pursued despite being forbidden to quarrel and stir up discord.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r3.anchor: وثالثها : أنهم نهوا عن التنازع وإثارة الفتن وهم كانوا مشتغلين بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r4.claim: The clearest sense of corruption is harm extending beyond its perpetrator, especially obstructing obedience to the Messenger; observance of the law establishes justice and social order.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r4.anchor: فالأظهر أن يراد به الفساد الذي يتعدى دون ما يقف عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r5.claim: Razi connects opposition to the Messenger with social corruption, citing Pharaoh’s fear that changing religion would spread corruption in the land.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r5.anchor: إنى أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر فى الارض الفساد

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r6.claim: One account of their loss is forfeiting their place in Paradise: each person has a place there, which the obedient attain and believers inherit from the disobedient.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r6.anchor: أنه لا أحد إلا وله في الجنة أهل ومنزل

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r7.claim: A second account is that unbelief cancels the good deeds of Jews and hypocrites, leaving no benefit or reward from those deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r7.anchor: خسروا حسناتهم التي عملوها لأنهم أحبطوها بكفرهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r8.claim: A third account is that they clung to unbelief to preserve immediate pleasures, only to lose them when fighting was permitted or when they died.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r8.anchor: إنما أصروا على الكفر خوفا من أن تفوتهم اللذات العاجلة

RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r9.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r9.claim: Qaffal defines loss generally as work that brings no recompense, like spending effort and receiving nothing of equal value; he links this to other verses about futile labor.
RAZI-FULL:v2p137/r9.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله تعالى : وبالجملة أن الخاسر اسم عام يقع على كل من عمل عملا لا يجزي عليه

STUDYQURAN:2:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r1.claim: One reading takes the Covenant as humanity’s general duty to acknowledge God’s Oneness and worship Him, grounded in the pre-eternal covenant.
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r1.anchor: the general obligation of human beings to acknowledge God’s Oneness and worship Him

STUDYQURAN:2:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r2.claim: Another reading identifies the Covenant with the Arabs’ oath to be more rightly guided if a warner came.
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r2.anchor: it refers to And they swore by God their most solemn oaths

STUDYQURAN:2:27/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r3.claim: A third interpretation takes the Covenant as a specific one made with the People of the Book.
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r3.anchor: or it refers to a specific covenant made with the People of the Book

STUDYQURAN:2:27/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r4.claim: Some understand what God commands to be joined as blood ties, whose reverence and maintenance are commanded elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r4.anchor: Some say that what God has commanded be joined refers to blood ties

STUDYQURAN:2:27/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r5.claim: Others understand the command to join broadly as any Divine Command to keep things joined.
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r5.anchor: Others consider it to include any such Divine Command to keep things joined

STUDYQURAN:2:27/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r6.claim: Some note that Jews also had blood ties to the Prophet because Isaac and Ishmael were brothers.
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r6.anchor: not only the Arabs had blood ties to the Prophet; the Jews did also

STUDYQURAN:2:27/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r7.claim: Khāsir can describe being deprived of something or being lost by losing one’s way or self.
STUDYQURAN:2:27/r7.anchor: khāsir can also denote “being lost” in the sense of losing one’s way or losing one’s self

TAB-FULL:v1p423/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p423/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p423/r1.claim: After God gave the two parables of the hypocrites, they objected that God was too exalted to offer such examples; the passage from the mosquito verse through the losers answered them.
TAB-FULL:v1p423/r1.anchor: لما ضرب الله هذين المثلين للمنافقين

TAB-FULL:v1p435/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r1.claim: Al-Tabari frames the broken-covenant point through competing definitions, beginning with the general view that the covenant is God’s charge to creation.
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r1.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هو وصية الله إلى خلقه، وأمره إياهم

TAB-FULL:v1p435/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r2.claim: One view takes the covenant as God’s commands and prohibitions delivered through scripture and messengers; breaking it means failing to act on them.
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r2.anchor: هو وصية الله إلى خلقه، وأمره إياهم بما أمرهم به من طاعته

TAB-FULL:v1p435/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r3.claim: Another view limits the passage to disbelieving and hypocritical People of the Book: they broke the Torah covenant to follow Muhammad and disclose what they knew about him.
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r3.anchor: هو ما أخذه الله عليهم في التوراة من العمل بما فيها

TAB-FULL:v1p435/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r4.claim: A broader view says all polytheists, disbelievers, and hypocrites break the covenant of monotheism and prophetic proof by rejecting what evidence shows to be true.
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r4.anchor: جميع أهل الشرك والكفر والنفاق وعهده إلى جميعهم في توحيده

TAB-FULL:v1p435/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r5.claim: Another view identifies the covenant as the pledge made when God brought Adam’s descendants forth; breaking it means failing to honor that pledge.
TAB-FULL:v1p435/r5.anchor: العهد الذي أخذه عليهم حين أخرجهم من صلب آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p437/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r1.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the passage initially concerns Jewish scholars in Medina and nearby Israelites, alongside hypocritical polytheists, while applying to everyone who follows their misguidance.
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r1.anchor: الآيات نزلت في كفار أحبار اليهود الذين كانوا بين ظهراني مهاجر رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v1p437/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r2.claim: The broken covenant is the known duty to affirm Muhammad and reveal his prophethood rather than conceal it, as the Torah pledge required.
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r2.anchor: التاركون ما عهد الله إليهم من الإقرار بمحمد

TAB-FULL:v1p437/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r3.claim: The immediate address is supported by the earlier descriptions of disbelievers and hypocrites and the later special address to the Children of Israel; the warning also reaches all peoples on their path.
TAB-FULL:v1p437/r3.anchor: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأوفوا بعهدي

TAB-FULL:v1p439/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r1.claim: After God’s confirmed covenant means after He had formally bound them to keep what He required; the word mīthāq is the noun from tawaththuqu, and its pronoun refers to God.
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r1.anchor: والميثاق اسم منه، والهاء في الميثاق عائدة على اسم الله.

TAB-FULL:v1p439/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r2.claim: The warning also includes anyone who breaks covenants, cuts ties, and spreads corruption in the same way as the hypocrites and disbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r2.anchor: كل من كان بالصفة التي وصف الله بها هؤلاء الفاسقين

TAB-FULL:v1p439/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r3.claim: Qatada warns against breaking the covenant: God hates it and threatens it, and anyone who gives God a sincere pledge must fulfill it.
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r3.anchor: فإياكم ونقض هذا الميثاق، فإن الله قد كره نقضه

TAB-FULL:v1p439/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r4.claim: When hypocrites have the upper hand they display six traits, adding covenant-breaking, severing ties, and corruption to lying, broken promises, and betrayal; when weakened they show the first three.
TAB-FULL:v1p439/r4.anchor: إذا كانت لهم الظهرة أظهروا هذه الخلال الست جميعا

TAB-FULL:v1p440/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r1.claim: What God commands people to join is kinship: relatives connected through one maternal line; severing it means unjustly withholding their due rights and kindness.
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r1.anchor: الذين جمعتهم وإياه رحم والدة واحدة، وقطع ذلك ظلمه

TAB-FULL:v1p440/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r2.claim: Grammatically, the relative expression with yuṣala is governed by the preposition’s implied genitive and refers back to the pronoun in bihi: what God ordered to be joined.
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r2.anchor: وأن التي مع يوصل في محل خفض بمعنى ردها على موضع الهاء

TAB-FULL:v1p440/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the severed ties as kinship and family relations.
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r3.anchor: فقطع والله ما أمر الله به أن يوصل بقطيعة الرحم والقرابة

TAB-FULL:v1p440/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r4.claim: A broader reading includes severing the Messenger, believers, and their relations; al-Tabari finds it plausible and concludes that every severing of what God ordered joined is condemned.
TAB-FULL:v1p440/r4.anchor: فهي دالة على ذم الله كل قاطع قطع ما أمر الله بوصله

TAB-FULL:v1p442/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r1.claim: Losers are those who diminish their own share of God’s mercy through disobedience, like merchants who lose capital; disbelievers and hypocrites lose mercy when they most need it at resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r1.anchor: الناقصون أنفسهم حظوظها بمعصيتهم الله من رحمته

TAB-FULL:v1p442/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r2.speaker: جرير بن عطية
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r2.claim: Jarir uses khusār for what diminishes people’s share of honor and nobility, illustrating the loss sense.
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r2.anchor: قال جرير بن عطية: [البحر الرجز] إن سليطا في الخسار

TAB-FULL:v1p442/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r3.claim: Some interpret the losers as the doomed; this can express the same loss of mercy without defining the word itself as doom.
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r3.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى {أولئك هم الخاسرون}

TAB-FULL:v1p442/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r4.claim: Labels such as loser applied to non-Muslims mean unbelief, while such labels applied to Muslims mean sin.
TAB-FULL:v1p442/r4.anchor: كل شيء نسبه الله إلى غير أهل الإسلام من اسم مثل خاسر

TABATABAI:2:26-27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī links these verses with the contrast in 13:19–21 between those who fulfill God's covenant and those who break it.
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية والتي بعدها نظيرة ما في سورة الرعد

TABATABAI:2:26-27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r4.claim: The Qur'an's descriptions imply that people have another happy or wretched life within worldly life, whose roots become visible when the veil is lifted.
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r4.anchor: للإنسان في الدنيا وراء الحياة التي يعيش بها فيها حياة أخرى سعيدة أو شقية

TABATABAI:2:26-27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r5.claim: The Qur'an also indicates a life before this world; worldly life lies between prior and later lives, each following the one before it.
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r5.anchor: أن للإنسان حياة قبل هذه الحياة الدنيا وحياة بعدها

TABATABAI:2:26-27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r6.speaker: الجمهور من المفسرين
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r6.claim: Most exegetes read descriptions of prior life as figurative states of disposition and descriptions of afterlife as metaphor, though many verses resist that reading.
TABATABAI:2:26-27/r6.anchor: الجمهور من المفسرين حملوا القسم الأول من الآيات وهي الواصفة للحياة السابقة

TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r1.claim: Many verses portray the afterlife as recompense in the form of the very deeds people performed, with numerous Qur'anic examples cited.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r1.anchor: كلامه تعالى موضوع على وجهين أحدهما وجه المجازاة بالثواب والعقاب

TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r2.claim: Qur'an 50:22 implies that what people see at resurrection was already present but hidden: heedlessness concerns something present, and a veil covers something that exists.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r2.anchor: إذ الغفلة لا تكون إلا عن معلوم حاضر، وكشف الغطاء لا يستقيم إلا عن مغطى موجود

TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an speaks both of recompense and of deeds taking embodied form; these accounts are compatible ways of bringing truths close to understanding.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r3.anchor: وإياك أن تتوهم أن الوجهين متنافيان، فإن الحقائق إنما تقرب إلى الأفهام بالأمثال المضروبة

TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r4.claim: Fāsiq is said to derive from a date slipping out of its skin; breaking a covenant follows its binding, and loss presupposes prior possession.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#2/r4.anchor: مأخوذ من فسقت التمرة إذا خرجت عن قشرها وجلدها

TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r1.claim: Qur'anic spiritual labels disclose real spiritual facts and stations, each producing its own effects and rulings; they are not casual rhetorical decoration.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r1.anchor: بل هي أوصاف كاشفة عن حقائق روحية ومقامات معنوية

TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r2.claim: God's absolute ownership permits every conceivable act in His creation without blame; human ownership is limited to actions rational society accepts.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#3/r2.anchor: وأما هو تعالى فكل تصرف تصرف به فهو تصرف من مالك وتصرف في مملوك

TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r1.claim: God alone disposes of His domain; every other agent acts only with His permission and will, as required by lordship.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r1.anchor: فالله هو المتصرف الفاعل في ملكه وليس لشيء غيره شيء من ذلك إلا بإذنه ومشيئته

TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r2.claim: In legislation God follows the rational community's distinctions between good and bad, praise and blame, and interests and harms.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r2.anchor: وفي ذلك إمضاء لطريقة العقلاء في المجتمع

TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r3.claim: Rational legislation and punishment serve real interests, and punishment should match a deed in kind and measure.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r3.anchor: وكل المجازاة إنما تكون بالمسانخة بين الجزاء وأصل العمل في الخيرية والشرية

TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r4.claim: Commands and prohibitions address only agents who can choose, and reward or punishment attaches to voluntary acts, except when one's own bad choice caused the constraint.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r4.anchor: أن الأمر والنهي وكل حكم تشريعي لا يتوجه إلا إلى المختار دون المضطر والمجبر على الفعل

TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r5.claim: If God compelled obedience and disobedience, reward would be arbitrary and punishment unjust, contrary to rational standards.
