TABATABAI:2:26-27#4/r5.anchor: لم يكن جزاء المطيع بالجنة والعاصي بالنار إلا جزافا

TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r1.claim: Legislation serves people's worldly and future interests, addresses them as agents who can choose, and rewards or punishes what they freely earn.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r1.anchor: فالتكاليف مجعولة على وفق مصالح العباد في معاشهم ومعادهم أولا

TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r2.claim: Divine misguidance, deception, scheming, and Satan's influence are forms of recompense and abandonment after a person freely turns toward evil, not initial deception.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r2.anchor: بل الثابت له الإضلال مجازاة وخذلانا لمن يستقبل بسوء اختياره ذلك

TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r3.claim: Divine decree concerns deeds as existent, not their attribution to human agents as actions; the author promises further explanation.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r3.anchor: القضاء غير متعلق بأفعال العباد من حيث أنها منسوبة إلى الفاعلين بالانتساب الفعلي دون الانتساب الوجودي

TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r4.claim: Legislation fits neither compulsion nor delegation: command is senseless if God owns none of an act, while delegation denies His unrestricted ownership.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#5/r4.anchor: مضافا إلى أن التفويض لا يتم إلا مع سلب إطلاق الملك منه تعالى عن بعض ما في ملكه

TABATABAI:2:26-27#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#6/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#6/r1.claim: After affirming that the journey occurred under divine decree, Ali rejects fatalistic compulsion: it would erase accountability; God assigned choice, warned people, and does not force either obedience or sin.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#6/r1.anchor: فقال له أمير المؤمنين أجل يا شيخ فوالله ما علوتم تلعة ولا هبطتم بطن واد إلا بقضاء من الله وقدر

TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r1.claim: The fatalist inference from eternal divine will makes every event necessary or impossible, apparently eliminating human choice, pre-act capacity, obligation, deserved reward, and deserved punishment.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r1.anchor: وحينئذ لم يكن معنى للقدرة قبل الفعل على الفعل، ولا معنى للتكليف لعدم القدرة قبل الفعل

TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r2.claim: On that fatalist account, some theologians deny objective good and evil and accept arbitrary preference, impossible duties, and punishment without fault; the author rejects these implications.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r2.anchor: والحسن والقبح أمران غير واقعيين لا يلزم تقيد أفعاله تعالى بهما

TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r3.claim: The sheikh's claim that he could only count his march as toil treats his intention as emptied of effect by divine will; Ali answers from the rational basis of responsibility.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r3.anchor: فهو الذي أتعبني بذلك فأجاب عنه الإمام عليه السلام بقوله لو كان كذلك لبطل الثواب والعقاب

TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r4.claim: Arbitrary creation would make the world purposeless and undo belief in resurrection; Ali's denial that anyone is overcome in sin or forced in obedience rules out compulsion.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#7/r4.anchor: وهذا الإمكان يساوق الوجوب، فلا غاية على هذا التقدير للخلقة والإيجاد

TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r1.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r1.claim: Al-Rida says God is neither obeyed by coercion nor disobeyed by overpowering; He owns people and their capacities, does not prevent obedience, and does not introduce people into sins He allows.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r1.anchor: عن الرضا عليه السلام قال ذكر عنده الجبر والتفويض فقال

TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r2.claim: The determinists correctly infer necessity when an act is measured against its complete cause, but wrongly apply it to a partial cause such as the human agent alone.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r2.anchor: الفعل الاختياري الصادر عن الإنسان بإرادته إذا فرض منسوبا إلى جميع ما يحتاج إليه في وجوده

TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r3.claim: Divine will and human will are vertically related: God's willing an act as voluntary requires the person's choice rather than cancelling it.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#8/r3.anchor: فالإرادة في طول الإرادة وليست في عرضها حتى تتزاحما

TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r1.claim: The Mu'tazilites affirm human choice but, sharing the fatalists' premise that divine willing cancels choice, deny God's will in human acts and thereby make humans independent creators.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r1.anchor: والمعتزلة وإن خالفت المجبرة في اختيارية أفعال العبد وسائر اللوازم

TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r2.claim: The sound account preserves both God's ownership and the servant's ownership in ordered ranks: the servant owns within God's ownership.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r2.anchor: فالمولى مالك في عين أن العبد مالك

TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r3.claim: In a report to Abaya ibn Ribi, Ali says human capacity is possessed through God: it is God's gift when granted and a trial when withdrawn.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#9/r3.anchor: فقال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام تملكها من دون الله أو مع الله

TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الثالث عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r1.claim: A report attributed to Abu al-Hasan III says that God would not disown people's sins if He had created them; God's disavowal concerns their shirk and evil, not their created bodies.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r1.anchor: وقد روي عن أبي الحسن الثالث عليه السلام أنه سئل عن أفعال العباد أهي مخلوقة لله تعالى

TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r2.claim: Acts have an aspect of existence and an aspect of attribution; their attribution to an agent determines whether they count as obedience, sin, good, or evil.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#10/r2.anchor: للأفعال جهتان جهة ثبوت ووجود، وجهة الانتساب إلى الفاعل

TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r1.claim: Sins are evil as absences of good, not created in that respect; misfortunes are evil only relative to a person who loses a blessing, while their existence is from God.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r1.anchor: فكل سيئة فهي أمر عدمي غير منسوب من هذه الجهة إلى الله سبحانه البتة

TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r2.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r2.claim: Al-Rida's report says human ability and blessings come from God, but people own their sins; God is more entitled to their good deeds than they are.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r2.anchor: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك

TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r3.claim: Abu Ja'far and Abu Abd Allah say God is too merciful to compel people to sin and punish them, yet too mighty to will something that fails to occur; a third position is broader than the distance between heaven and earth.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r3.anchor: وفي التوحيد عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليه السلام " قالا إن الله عز وجل أرحم بخلقه من أن يجبر خلقه

TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r4.claim: Ibn Ajlan's report says God is too generous to delegate all agency to people and too just to compel an act and then punish its agent.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r4.anchor: وفي التوحيد عن محمد بن عجلان، قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام فوض الله الأمر إلى العباد؟

TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r5.claim: In Mihzam's report, al-Sadiq denies both compulsion and delegation; he explains that God brings about voluntary acts through human choice without overpowering it.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#11/r5.anchor: وفي التوحيد أيضا عن مهزم، قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام أخبرني عما اختلف فيه من خلفك

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r1.claim: The Prophet says that claiming God commands evil lies about Him, while claiming good and evil fall outside His will removes Him from sovereignty.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r1.anchor: من زعم أن الله يأمر بالسوء والفحشاء فقد كذب على الله

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r2.claim: Hasan al-Basri reports Ali's view that a person was not misled by the one who forbade sin; the person's own self misled him, and God is free of that.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r2.anchor: الحسن البصري أن أحسن ما انتهى إلي ما سمعت أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبى طالب عليه السلام، أنه قال " أتظن أن الذي نهاك دهاك

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r3.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd reports Ali's argument that if wrongdoing were fixed from the beginning, the wrongdoer punished for it would be unjustly treated.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r3.anchor: أحسن ما سمعت في القضاء والقدر قول أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام " لو كان الزور في الأصل محتوما

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r4.claim: Wasil ibn Ata reports Ali asking whether God would show a path and then impose a constricted passage, rejecting a fatalistic account.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r4.anchor: أحسن ما سمعت في القضاء والقدر قول أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام " أيدلك على الطريق ويأخذ عليك المضيق

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r5.claim: Amir al-Sha'bi reports Ali's distinction: what people seek God's forgiveness for belongs to them, while what they praise God for comes from Him.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r5.anchor: أحسن ما سمعت في القضاء والقدر قول أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام " كلما استغفرت الله منه فهو منك

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r6.speaker: الحجاج بن يوسف
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r6.claim: After reading the four answers on decree and destiny, al-Hajjaj praises them as coming from a pure source.

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r7.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r7.claim: Al-Sadiq says acts one can blame a servant for are the servant's, whereas illness, shortness, and skin color are God's acts.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r7.anchor: جعفر بن محمد الصادق عليه السلام عن القضاء والقدر فقال " ما استطعت أن تلوم العبد عليه فهو منه

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r8.claim: A report in Nahj al-Balagha defines divine unity as not imagining God and justice as not accusing Him.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r8.anchor: وفي النهج سئل عليه السلام عن التوحيد والعدل؟ فقال " التوحيد أن لا تتوهمه

TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r9.claim: The reports use several arguments: command and recompense presume choice, and Qur'anic claims about divine ownership, justice, and not commanding indecency exclude compulsion or delegation.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#12/r9.anchor: الاستدلال بنفس الأمر والنهي والعقاب والثواب وأمثالها على تحقق الاختيار

TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r1.claim: The Qur'an's statement that God does not command indecency stands even if an act would not be called indecent when attributed to God, because the verse specifically denies that command.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r1.anchor: فالإشارة بقوله بهذا يوجب أن يكون النفي اللاحق متوجها إليه

TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r2.claim: Divine names and attributes such as powerful, merciful, and generous do not hold their meanings under either compulsion or delegation.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r2.anchor: وهذه صفات لا تستقر معانيها إلا عند ما يكون وجود كل شيء منه تعالى

TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r3.claim: Repentance and blame make sense only if wrong belongs to the agent; they would be pointless if every act came wholly from God.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r3.anchor: فإن الذنب لو لم يكن من العبد لم يكن معنى لاستغفار

TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r4.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r4.claim: Al-Rida explains that God does not abandon people as creatures might; when He knows they will persist in disbelief, He withholds help and leaves them to their own choice.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r4.anchor: عن الرضا عليه السلام في قوله تعالى وتركهم في ظلمات لا يبصرون

TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r5.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r5.claim: Al-Rida explains the sealing of disbelievers' hearts as punishment for their disbelief, citing the Qur'an's statement that disbelief sealed them.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#13/r5.anchor: قال الختم هو الطبع على قلوب الكفار عقوبة على كفرهم

TABATABAI:2:26-27#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#14/r2.claim: Kinds in the external world are inferred from their distinct effects: senses perceive effects, and reason infers their causes and underlying subjects.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#14/r2.anchor: فإنا إنما أثبتنا وجود هذه الأنواع ونوعيتها الممتازة عن غيرها من طريق الآثار والأفاعيل

TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r1.claim: Actions divide into natural acts that arise without knowledge directing them and conscious acts, such as human and animal choices, whose knowledge identifies the act as the agent's perfection.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r1.anchor: الفعل الصادر عن الطبيعة من غير دخل للعلم في صدوره

TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r2.claim: Habits, bodily nature, or overpowering emotion can yield action without deliberation; when several images of an act are possible, the agent weighs them, then acts once one is selected.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#15/r2.anchor: وأما الأفعال التي لها صور علمية متعددة تكون هي من جهة بعضها مصداق كمال الإنسان

TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r1.claim: Voluntary acts may be freely selected or performed under threat; even a coerced person acts after judging action preferable to inaction, so the two are not essentially different kinds.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r1.anchor: فخرج خائفا عد فعله هذا إجباريا من غير فرق بين الفعلين والترجيحين أصلا

TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r2.claim: Praise, blame, and recompense distinguish choice from coercion through rational social conventions, not through different external essences; the question therefore needs a different philosophical argument.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r2.anchor: فهي آثار اعتبارية غير حقيقية، فليس البحث عن الجبر والاختيار بحثا فلسفيا

TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r3.claim: Every possible existent depends on a cause and becomes necessary once its complete cause is present; the whole chain of existence is necessary in that relation.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#16/r3.anchor: ولا شك أيضا أن الشيء ما لم يجب لم يوجد

TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r1.claim: An effect is necessary relative to its complete cause but possible relative to a partial cause; this yields systems of necessity and possibility in nature.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r1.anchor: أما إذا نسب المعلول المذكور إلى بعض أجزاء العلة أو إلى شيء آخر

TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r2.claim: A human voluntary act is necessary relative to all its causes and conditions, but possible relative to the human agent alone.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r2.anchor: فإذا فرضت فعلا من أفعال الإنسان الاختيارية ونسبتها إلى تمام علتها

TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r3.claim: Against the Mu'tazilites, human beings and their deeds depend on God for existence with all their particulars; divine willing includes the deed as freely chosen, contrary to the fatalist claim that it cancels choice.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#17/r3.anchor: فالحق الحقيق بالتصديق أن الأفعال الإنسانية لها نسبة إلى الفاعل ونسبة إلى الواجب

TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r1.claim: The author rejects materialist determinism: an act is necessary relative to its complete cause but remains possible relative to a partial cause such as its agent.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r1.anchor: فما ذكره جمع من الماديين من فلاسفة العصر الحاضر من شمول الجبر لنظام الطبيعة وإنكار الاختيار باطل جدا

TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r2.claim: Human planning, education, and hope presume that acts remain possible relative to their agents; these practices would make no sense for necessities.
TABATABAI:2:26-27#18/r2.anchor: فبنائه في جميع مواقف عمله على أساس الرجاء والتربية والتعليم

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r1.claim: In ماذا, ما and ذا may form one noun in the accusative (‘what did God intend by this example?’), or ذا may be a relative pronoun, with ما as the subject and ذا as its predicate.
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r1.anchor:
وقوله (ماذا) يجوز أن يكون (ما) و (ذا) اسما واحدا يكون موضعهما
نصبا

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r2.claim: الفاسقين is accusative by ellipsis: the sense is ‘He misguides none by it except the defiantly disobedient.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r2.anchor:
وإعراب (الفاسقين) نصب كأن المعنى وما يضل به أحد إلا
الفاسقين.

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r3.claim: The covenant is most plausibly the pledge taken from prophets and their followers to believe in and support the confirming Messenger; إصر means ‘My covenant.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r3.anchor:
(عهد الله) هنا - والله أعلم - ما أخذ الله على النبيين ومن اتبعهم ألا
يكفروا بأمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -،

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r4.claim: Another possible covenant is the one taken from Adam’s descendants, who acknowledged God as Lord.
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r4.anchor:
ويجوز أن يكون عهد الله الذي أخذه من بني آدم من ظهورهم.
حين قال. . . (وأشهدهم على أنفسهم

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r5.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r5.claim: Some say God’s covenant is the rational evidence for His oneness: every discerning person knows God is Creator and must believe in Him.
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r5.anchor: وقال قوم أن عهد الله - عز وجل - الاستدلال على توحيده، وأن كل ذي تمييز يعلم أن الله

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r6.claim: The first two covenant interpretations are supported by Qur’anic passages that confirm their explanation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r6.anchor: والقولان الأولان في القرآن ما يصدق تفسيرهما

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r7.claim: الذين is accusative as an adjective of الفاسقين; أن يوصل is genitive as an appositive to the pronoun in به.
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r7.anchor:
فأما إعراب (الذين) فالنصب على الصفة للفاسقين، وموضع قوله:
(أن يوصل) خفض على البدل من الهاء

ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r8.claim: أولئك is the subject and الخاسرون its predicate; هم may be a separating pronoun (called عماد by Kufans), or a second subject in a second valid parse.
ZAJJAJ:v1p105/r8.anchor:
و (الخاسرون) خبر الابتداء وهم بمعنى
الفصل وهو الذي يسميه الكوفيون العماد، ويجوز أن يكون أولئك رفعا

TABRISI:2:27/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r1.claim: نقض is the opposite of confirming a bond; عهد can mean a covenant, binding pledge, or God's command and instruction.
TABRISI:2:27/r1.anchor: النقض نقيض الإبرام والعهد العقد والعهد الموثق

TABRISI:2:27/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r2.claim: A covenant is God's instruction, as in the address ألم أعهد إليكم بني آدم.
TABRISI:2:27/r2.anchor: وعهد الله وصيته وأمره يقال عهد الخليفة إلى فلان بكذا

TABRISI:2:27/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r3.claim: Mīthāq is the thing by which a pledge is made binding; qaṭʿ originally divides physical things and extends metaphorically to speech and matters.
TABRISI:2:27/r3.anchor: والميثاق ما وقع التوثيق به كما أن الميقات ما وقع التوقيت به

TABRISI:2:27/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r4.claim: The command form fundamentally requests action, though it can express permission, threat, challenge, or creative fiat.
TABRISI:2:27/r4.anchor: والأصل في الجميع الطلب والوصل نقيض الفصل

TABRISI:2:27/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r5.claim: Loss is diminution or destruction, and the root idea is losing one's capital.

TABRISI:2:27/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r6.claim: الذين ينقضون is an accusative adjective describing the previously mentioned evildoers; أولئك begins the next clause and الخاسرون is its predicate.
TABRISI:2:27/r6.anchor: الذين ينقضون في موضع النصب لأنها صفة الفاسقين وأولئك مبتدأ

TABRISI:2:27/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r7.claim: The min in من بعد may be extra or mark a starting point; the suffix in ميثاقه may refer to the covenant or to God.
TABRISI:2:27/r7.anchor: من مزيدة وقيل معناه ابتداء الغاية والهاء في ميثاقه عائد إلى العهد

TABRISI:2:27/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r8.claim: The phrase أن يوصل appositionally explains the pronoun in به: what God commanded to be joined.
TABRISI:2:27/r8.anchor: أن يوصل بدل من الهاء التي في به

TABRISI:2:27/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r9.claim: One view takes the covenant as rational evidence for divine unity and justice and prophetic proofs; breaking it means refusing what reason showed to be true.
TABRISI:2:27/r9.anchor: أنه ركب في عقولهم من أدلة التوحيد والعدل وتصديق الرسل

TABRISI:2:27/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r10.claim: Another view understands God's covenant as the commands and prohibitions delivered by His messenger; breaking it means failing to act on them.
TABRISI:2:27/r10.anchor: أنه وصية الله إلى خلقه على لسان رسوله بما أمرهم به من طاعته

TABRISI:2:27/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r11.speaker: الطبري
TABRISI:2:27/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the view that the covenant was the People of the Book's pledge in the Torah to follow Muhammad and disclose the truth, which they knowingly concealed.

TABRISI:2:27/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27/r12.claim: The view that the covenant was taken when humanity was brought from Adam's loins is weak: God cannot bind people by an unknown pledge without evidence.
TABRISI:2:27/r12.anchor: وهذا الوجه ضعيف لأنه لا يجوز أن يحتج على عباده بعهد لا يذكرونه

TABRISI:2:27#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:27#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the severed relationship is ties with the Prophet and believers, whom the breakers were ordered to maintain.
TABRISI:2:27#2/r1.anchor: أمروا بصلة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين فقطعوهم عن الحسن

TABRISI:2:27#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:27#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says it is kinship and family ties that they were commanded to keep.
TABRISI:2:27#2/r2.anchor: أمروا بصلة الرحم والقرابة فقطعوها عن قتادة

TABRISI:2:27#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27#2/r3.claim: Other views understand the severed command as belief in all prophets and scriptures, or as joining words to deeds rather than professing without acting.
TABRISI:2:27#2/r3.anchor: وقيل أمروا بالإيمان بجميع الأنبياء والكتب ففرقوا وقطعوا ذلك

TABRISI:2:27#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27#2/r4.claim: The broadest interpretation is to include everyone God commands people to join among His allies; cutting them off means repudiating and rejecting them.
TABRISI:2:27#2/r4.anchor: وهذا أقوى لأنه أعم ويدخل فيه الجميع

TABRISI:2:27#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27#2/r5.claim: Corruption on earth has been explained as calling people to unbelief, frightening travelers and blocking roads, or breaking God's covenant.
TABRISI:2:27#2/r5.anchor: قال قوم استدعاؤهم إلى الكفر هو الفساد في الأرض وقيل إخافتهم السبيل

TABRISI:2:27#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:27#2/r6.claim: The best reading generalizes corruption to every sin whose harm extends beyond its perpetrator; the breakers destroy themselves and lose their capital.
TABRISI:2:27#2/r6.anchor: أي اهلكوا أنفسهم فهم بمنزلة من هلك رأس ماله

TABRISI:2:27#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:27#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:27#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says loss attributed to non-Muslims means unbelief, while loss attributed to Muslims means worldly loss.
TABRISI:2:27#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن كل ما نسبه الله تعالى من الخسار إلى غير المسلمين

THALABI:v1p173/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r1.claim: They break the covenant by abandoning or opposing it; the root of naqḍ means breaking.
THALABI:v1p173/r1.anchor: الذين ينقضون أي يتركون ويخالفون، وأصل النقض: الكسر

THALABI:v1p173/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r2.claim: God's covenant is His command at the primordial pledge and the Torah's command to believe in Muhammad with his description.
THALABI:v1p173/r2.anchor: عهد الله أمره الذي عهد إليهم يوم الميثاق

THALABI:v1p173/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r3.claim: Mithaq means confirmation and reinforcement, derived from a word for a firm bond.
THALABI:v1p173/r3.anchor: من بعد ميثاقه توكيده وتشديده، وهو مفعال من الوثيقة

THALABI:v1p173/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r4.claim: One explanation of severing what God ordered joined is breaking kinship ties.
THALABI:v1p173/r4.anchor: ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل يعني الأرحام

THALABI:v1p173/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r5.claim: Another explanation is refusing to believe in all messengers and books: Jews sever by accepting some and rejecting others, while believers join them by making no distinction.
THALABI:v1p173/r5.anchor: وقال المؤمنون: لا نفرق بين أحد

THALABI:v1p173/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r6.claim: Their corruption consists of sins and obstructing people from believing in Muhammad and the Qur'an.
THALABI:v1p173/r6.anchor: ويفسدون في الأرض بالمعاصي وتعويق الناس عن الإيمان بمحمد

THALABI:v1p173/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r7.claim: They are losers because they incur punishment and forfeit reward.
THALABI:v1p173/r7.anchor: أولئك هم الخاسرون: أي المغبونون بالعقوبة وفوت المثوبة

ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r1.claim: The bond with God is the moral duty to use one’s innate intellectual and physical gifts as God intended.
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r1.anchor: man's moral obligation to use his inborn gifts - intellectual as well as physical - in the way intended

ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r2.claim: Reason establishes this bond by revealing human weakness and dependence on a causal power, leading gradually to awareness of God’s will for conduct.
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r2.anchor: faculty of reason which, if properly used, must lead man to a realization of his own weakness and dependence

ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r3.claim: Because the passage names no particular covenant, Asad reads the bond as an innate human relationship with God, recognizable by instinct and experience.
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r3.anchor: there is no mention of any specific "covenant" in either the preceding or the subsequent verses

ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r4.claim: Asad links this innate relationship to God’s nearness to humanity and directs readers to his explanation of what God commands people to join.
ASAD-NOTES:2:26#n19/r4.anchor: namely, that innate relationship with God which makes Him "closer to man than his neck-vein" (50:16)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r1.claim: Alladhīna describes al-fāsiqīn; naqḍ means undoing a firmly made rope or building, and poetic naqāʾiḍ are poems that answer and undo another poet’s poem, including those of Jarīr and al-Farazdaq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r1.anchor: (والذين) من صفة الفاسقين. و (النقض) في # اللغة: الهدم، وإفساد ما أبرمته من حبل أو بناء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r2.claim: ʿAhd here can mean a testament or command, as in 36:60, or the binding covenant that secures what follows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r2.anchor: والذي أريد به هاهنا الوصية (¬10) والأمر من قولهم: عهد الخليفة إلى فلان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq offers two covenants: the demand that prophets and followers not reject Muhammad, linked to 3:81, or the primordial covenant with Adam’s descendants in 7:172.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r3.anchor: أحدهما: ما أخذه على النبيين ومن اتبعهم ألا يكفروا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r4.claim: The prophetic covenant is stronger because God would not hold people to an unknown proof; the Adam covenant also holds because revelation made it known as if remembered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r4.anchor: والوجه الأول أصحهما، من قبل أن الله لا يحتج عليهم بما لا يعرفون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the covenant in 13:25 with God’s covenant in Adam’s loins, when the descendants answered that God is their Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p282/r5.anchor: وهذا (¬1) الوجه هو قول ابن عباس ذكره في قوله: {والذين ينقضون عهد الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r1.claim: The mīm in min baʿdi is emphatic; mīthāq is what confirms something, and its yāʾ comes from wāw.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {من بعد ميثاقه}. (من) صلة لأجل التأكيد (¬4). والميثاق: ما وقع التوثيق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives miyāthiq and mawāthiq as plurals of mīthāq and cites a verse using miyāthiq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: يقال في جمع الميثاق: مياثق ومواثق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r3.claim: The pronoun in mīthāq can refer to God, meaning God’s confirmation of the covenant, or to the covenant itself, meaning its confirmation and reinforcement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p285/r3.anchor: والكناية في الميثاق يجوز أن تكون (¬7) عائدة على الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r1.claim: One interpretation of severing what God ordered joined is severing kinship; Quraysh cut their relationship with the Prophet through hostility.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r1.anchor: يعني الأرحام (¬1)، وذلك أن قريشا قطعوا رحم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالمعاداة معه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r2.claim: Another interpretation is rejecting some messengers and scriptures while accepting others, as in 4:150; Ibn ʿAbbās says believers join their belief by not distinguishing among God’s messengers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r2.anchor: وهذا الوجه هو قول ابن عباس ذكره في الآية التي في (الرعد) (¬3)، وقال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses an yūṣala as genitive apposition to the pronoun in mā, meaning what God commanded to be joined.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: وموضع {أن يوصل} خفض على، (¬5) البدل من (الهاء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r4.claim: Corruption on earth means disobedience and obstructing people from believing in Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r4.anchor: بالمعاصي، وتعويق الناس عن الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r5.claim: Losers first refers to losing capital in commerce; by extension these people lost the good they would have gained through faith, earned punishment, and missed reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p287/r5.anchor: القوم نقصوا (¬4) بكفرهم راحة أنفسهم التي كانت لهم لو آمنوا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r1.claim: The covenant is God’s command in earlier scriptures to believe in Muhammad, confirmed as obligatory; cutting what should be joined means Quraysh’s hostile rupture of kinship with the Prophet.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r1.anchor: وصيته وأمره في الكتب المتقدمة بالإيمان بمحمد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r2.claim: They corrupt the earth through sins and by obstructing people from believing in Muhammad; they lose reward and incur punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r2.anchor: بالـمعاصي وتعويق الناس عن الإيمان بمحمد

ELMALILI:2:27/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r1.claim: Breaking what God commands to be joined means failing to do righteous deeds and acting against divine commands and laws that secure rectitude; sins and major sins spread corruption on earth.

ELMALILI:2:27/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r2.claim: Fisq literally means going out, as mice leaving holes are called fawasiq; religiously it means leaving obedience through major sins, including persistence in minor sins.

ELMALILI:2:27/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r3.claim: Fisq has three degrees: occasional sin while recognizing its ugliness, habitual immersion in it, and committing it while denying its ugliness; only the third is unbelief.
ELMALILI:2:27/r3.anchor: Birincisi günahı çirkin addetmekle beraber ahyânen irtikâb etmek, ikincisi üzerine düşerek inhimak ile yapmak, üçüncüsü çirkinliğini inkâr ederek yapmaktır

ELMALILI:2:27/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r4.claim: In Sunni doctrine, a sinner retains the name believer until the unbelieving degree; Mu'tazilites place such a person between believer and unbeliever, while Kharijites call all three degrees unbelief.
ELMALILI:2:27/r4.anchor: bu kısmı ne mü’min ne kâfir ikisi ortası

ELMALILI:2:27/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r5.claim: The people called transgressors here are unquestionably unbelievers because they combine covenant-breaking, rejection of divine commands, and corruption through forbidden acts; the preceding verse's disbelievers' response to the parable reinforces this.
ELMALILI:2:27/r5.anchor: Allah’a verdiği ahdi nakz edip akidesini bozmak, emr-i ilâhînin aksini yapmak, menâhîyi irtikâb ile de yeryüzünü fesâda vermek

ELMALILI:2:27/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r6.claim: A key shift is that the earlier contrast was faith versus unbelief, while this passage sets faith and righteous action against fisq; rejection or misinterpretation of Quranic parables is tied to intellectual and practical aspects of transgression.
ELMALILI:2:27/r6.anchor: yalnız iman ve küfür tekabülü esas iken burada hem iman ve hem amel-i sâlih mecmû‘una mukabil olmak üzere ayrıca da fısk

ELMALILI:2:27/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r7.claim: The intellectual root of unbelief is bad interpretation, deliberate or ignorant, often directed at parables and ambiguous passages, and it usually accompanies practical unbelief; the Quran affirms parables as true and necessary to its style.
ELMALILI:2:27/r7.anchor: temsîlâtın da mevcûdiyetini ve bunun esası olan hak nokta-i nazarına muhalif değil, belki lâzım bulunduğunu

ELMALILI:2:27/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r8.claim: Araf 7:53 depicts those who forgot the promised interpretation recognizing the messengers' truth only when it arrives, then finding their inventions gone and themselves lost; accept true parables, act, and let events disclose their interpretation.
ELMALILI:2:27/r8.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh temsîlât-ı hakka inan, matlub olan ameli yap, tevilini istikbale, cereyân-ı hâdisâta bırak

ELMALILI:2:27/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r9.claim: Fisq entails either unbelief or ingratitude and ends in loss; after condemning it in the third person, the discourse turns to direct address for guidance.
ELMALILI:2:27/r9.anchor: Hulâsa, fısk, ya küfrü veya küfrânı mutazammındır ve neticesi hüsrandır

ELMALILI:2:27/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:27/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:27/r10.claim: The losers are the whole class deprived of gain, whose work consists entirely of loss.
ELMALILI:2:27/r10.anchor: Kazançtan mahrum, işi gücü zarar ve ziyan olan kimseler diye asıl bunlara denilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r1.claim: The broken covenant may be the primordial pledge to recognize God as Lord and serve Him, answered affirmatively at the sacred gathering, or promises made in worldly relations while invoking God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r2.claim: Breaking promises is characteristic of hypocrites and others who share their traits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r2.anchor: Münafıkların ve onların özelliklerini paylaşan diğerlerinin âdetlerinden biri de verdikleri sözde durmamalarıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r3.speaker: Bazı tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r3.claim: Some exegetes restrict what God commands to be joined to particular bonds, such as kinship ties and reconciliation between spouses.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r4.claim: The author prefers a broader reading: God wills the unification of religions, prophets, books, and humanity through monotheism, the reconciliation of fragmented things, and each person or thing occupying its proper place.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r4.anchor: Doğrusu bunu daha geniş bir çerçevede almak ve anlamaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r5.claim: Corruptors, sinners, and wrongdoers work to divide and fragment what should be joined.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r5.anchor: Düzen bozucular (fesatçılar) ve günahkârlar (fâsıklar, zalimler) ise bunları parçalamak ve ayırmakla meşguldürler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r6.claim: Corruption on earth includes material and spiritual disorder, pollution, unrest, pain, and calamity, historically caused largely by unbelievers, immoral people, tyrants, and sinners.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r6.anchor: maddî ve mânevî olarak düzeni bozan, çevreyi kirleten, huzursuzluk, acı ve felâketlere sebep olanlar genellikle inkârcılar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r7.claim: Every sin is also corruption because it is forbidden by God and disrupts the earth's balance and order.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r7.anchor: aynı zamanda yeryüzünde bir kötülüktür, fesattır, dengeyi ve düzeni bozmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r8.claim: Those who serve ego and Satan instead of God inevitably lose: they spend their lifespan on a transient world and forfeit eternal bliss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:27/r8.anchor: ömür sermayesiyle fâni dünyayı satın almışlar, ebedî saadetten mahrum kalmışlardır

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r6.claim: نقض is undoing a constructed thing and returning it to its former state; عهد is a binding pledge with six Arabic senses: charge, guarantee, command, meeting, sight, and abode.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r6.anchor: النقض: فك تركيب الشيء ورده إلى ما كان عليه أولا، فنقض البناء هدمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r7.claim: ميثاق is a covenant reinforced by oath; it and توثقة resemble ميعاد and ميلاد in forming nouns of action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r7.anchor: والميثاق: العهد المؤكد باليمين. والميثاق والتوثقة: كالميعاد بمعنى الوعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r8.claim: خسار means diminution or destruction. كيف is mainly interrogative; conditional use is rare and Arabic does not attest its jussive, so analogy is rejected against the Kufans and Quṭrub.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r8.anchor: الخسار: النقصان أو الهلاك، كيف: اسم، ودخول حرف الجر عليها شاذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r9.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r9.claim: Grammarians disagree whether كيف is an adverb, attributed to Sībawayh, or a non-adverb noun, attributed to al-Akhfash and al-Sīrāfī; its answer takes case according to the verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r9.anchor: أهي ظرف أم اسم غير ظرف؟ والأول عزوه إلى سيبويه، والثاني إلى الأخفش والسيرافي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r1.claim: الذين ينقضون may be accusative as an adjective or detached censure, or nominative as a detached clause or subject; attaching it as an adjective is best because the other parses disconnect the sentence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r1.anchor: فالنصب من وجهين: إما على الاتباع، وإما على القطع، أي أذم الذين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r2.claim: This is a necessary blameworthy trait: every fāsiq breaks the covenant and severs what God commanded to be joined.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r2.anchor: وتكون هذه الصفة صفة ذم، وهي لازمة، إذ كل فاسق ينقض العهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r3.claim: One view identifies the covenant as God's charge to obey Him and avoid disobedience in revealed books and prophetic teaching; violation means failing to act on it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r3.anchor: أنه وصية الله إلى خلقه، وأمره لهم بطاعته، ونهيه لهم عن معصيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r4.claim: A second view identifies it as the primordial covenant taken from descendants, breached through denying God's lordship and the rights of His blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r4.anchor: أنه العهد الذي أخذه الله عليهم حين أخرجهم من أصلاب آبائهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r5.claim: A third view identifies the covenant as scriptural acknowledgment of God's oneness and favors and belief in His messengers; Jews breached it by discarding scripture and altering the Prophet's description.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r5.anchor: ما أخذه الله عليهم في الكتب المنزلة من الإقرار بتوحيده والاعتراف بنعمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r6.claim: A fourth view says God covenanted with prophets and their followers to believe, support, and honor the Prophet; its breach is denial of his mission or alteration of his description.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r6.anchor: ما أخذه الله تعالى على الأنبياء ومتبعيهم أن لا يكفروا بالله ولا بالنبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r7.claim: A fifth view says the covenant was prior faith in Muḥammad and his message, breached by denying his prophethood and attributes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r7.anchor: إيمانهم به صلى الله عليه وسلم ورسالته قبل بعثه ونقضهم له جحدهم لنبوته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r8.claim: A sixth view identifies the covenant with rational evidence for God's oneness and the Messenger's truth, breached by refusing to consider signs and blindly following forebears.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r8.anchor: ما جعله في عقولهم من الحجة على توحيده وتصديق رسوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r9.claim: A seventh view identifies it as the trust offered to the heavens and earth and carried by humanity; breach means failing its obligations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r9.anchor: الأمانة المعروضة على السموات والأرض التي حملها الإنسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r10.claim: An eighth view treats the covenant as the prohibition on killing and expelling one another; returning to those acts indicates that the addressees are Israelites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r10.anchor: ما أخذه عليهم من أن لا يسفكوا دماءهم ولا يخرجوا أنفسهم من ديارهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r11.claim: A ninth view makes the covenant faith and commitment to revealed law, with breach being apostasy after belief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205/r11.anchor: هو الإيمان والتزام الشرائع، ونقضه كفره بعد الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.claim: The nine covenant readings divide between universal and specific audiences, reflecting disagreement about the occasion; Abū Ḥayyān prefers the general sense, including every group that breaks God's covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.anchor: والعموم هو الظاهر. فكل من نقض عهد الله من مسلم وكافر ومنافق أو مشرك أو كتابي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.claim: من attaches to ينقضون as a starting point and shows the breach followed immediately after covenant confirmation, displaying disregard for it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.anchor: ومن متعلقة بقوله ينقضون، وهي لابتداء الغاية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r3.claim: The suggestion that من is extra is far-fetched.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.claim: ميثاق ordinarily denotes a covenant strengthened by firmness of binding, but here it figuratively means commitment and acceptance rather than an oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.anchor: والميثاق مفعول من الوثاقة، وهو الشد في العقد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls ميثاق a verbal noun in place of its مصدر and cites a line meaning after your giving.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو محمد بن عطية: هو اسم في موضع المصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Ibn ʿAṭiyya's account is not necessary; al-Zamakhsharī's after-the-confirmation reading works by analogy with ميعاد and ميلاد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.anchor: ولا يتعين ما ذكر، بل قد أجاز الزمخشري أن يكون بعد التوثقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r7.claim: Although forms on مفعال are usually intensive descriptors, Ibn al-Ḥājj and Ibn Mālik omit مفعال from their catalogs of verbal-noun patterns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r7.anchor: والأصل في مفعال أن يكون وصفا نحو: مطعام ومسقام ومذكار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r8.claim: The pronoun in ميثاقه most naturally refers to العهد, the topic; it may instead refer to God as the one who bound the covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r8.anchor: والضمير في ميثاقه عائد على العهد لأنه المحدث عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r9.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says a divine antecedent makes the مصدر active, whereas an antecedent of covenant makes it passive, implying that ميثاق is a verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: إن أعدت الهاء على اسم الله كان المصدر مضافا إلى الفاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says what God commanded to be joined is the Messenger, severed through denial and disobedience; Abū Ḥayyān objects that the wording should then be من rather than ما.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r10.anchor: أنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قطعوه بالتكذيب والعصيان، قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r11.claim: A second view takes the object as speech: hypocrites say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, and fail to join speech with action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r11.anchor: القول: أمر الله أن يوصل بالعمل فقطعوا بينهما، قالوا: ولم يعملوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r12.claim: A third view identifies it as affirming all prophets, which the breakers severed by denying some while accepting others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r12.anchor: التصديق بالأنبياء، أمروا بوصله فقطعوه بتكذيب بعض وتصديق بعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r13.claim: Qatāda identifies it as kinship ties, suggesting the immediate audience was Quraysh polytheists and similar groups.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r13.anchor: الرحم والقرابة، قاله قتادة، وهذا يدل على أنه أراد كفار قريش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the general reading: everything God commanded to be joined is included, with no clear evidence for narrowing the wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p205#2/r14.anchor: أنه على العموم في كل ما أمر الله به أن يوصل، وهذا هو الأوجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows ما to be an indefinite noun described by a clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r1.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء أن تكون ما نكرة موصوفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parsing because they sever something God commanded joined is too unrestricted to explain the severe verdict of sin and loss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r2.anchor: خصوصا هنا، إذ يصير المعنى: ويقطعون شيئا أمر الله به أن يوصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r3.claim: An أمر is a superior's request that an inferior perform an act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r3.anchor: والأمر هو استدعاء الأعلى الفعل من الأدنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī adds that an أمر prompts action and connects the noun meaning thing to the idea of something commanded; Abū Ḥayyān calls this an astute Muʿtazilī point.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وبعثه عليه، وهي نكتة اعتزالية لطيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r5.claim: The first object of أمر is understood, and أن يوصل is genitive as a substitute for the pronoun in به, meaning what God commanded them to join; poetry supports this analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r5.anchor: وأن يوصل في موضع جر بدل من الضمير في به تقديره به وصله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r6.speaker: المهدوي، وابن عطية، وأبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r6.claim: They allow أن يوصل as an accusative appositive to ما, yielding the joining of what God commanded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r6.anchor: وأجاز المهدوي وابن عطية وأبو البقاء أن تكون أن يوصل في موضع نصب بدلا من ما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r7.speaker: المهدوي وابن عطية وأبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r7.claim: They also allow a purpose clause, construed as because they dislike it being joined or lest it be joined; Abū al-Baqāʾ additionally allows a nominative predicate analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r7.anchor: وأجاز المهدوي وابن عطية أن تكون في موضع نصب مفعولا من أجله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls all these alternative parses weak and prefers his analysis as proper for the eloquent Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r8.anchor: وهذه الأعاريب كلها ضعيفة، ولولا شهرة قائلها لضربت عن ذكرها صفحا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r9.claim: فساد in the land is variously read as promoting unbelief, frightening and blocking travelers, covenant-breaking, or any sin whose harm reaches others; Ibn ʿAṭiyya adds idolatry and acting by desire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p207/r9.anchor: فيه أربعة أقوال: أحدها: استدعاؤهم إلى الكفر، والترغيب فيه، وحمل الناس عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r1.claim: The passage uses antithesis in small versus greater, believers versus disbelievers, guidance versus misguidance, covenant-breaking after confirmation, and cutting after connection; these last pairs express reversal of an earlier state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r1.anchor: ووقع هنا في قوله تعالى: بعوضة فما فوقها، فإنهما دليلان على الحقير والكبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r2.claim: The sequence of misguidance after guidance is illustrated by the report that each child is born in a natural state, and by reports that children dying before maturity enter Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r2.anchor: فالضلال بعد الهداية لقوله: كل مولود يولد على الفطرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r3.claim: The repeated imperfect verbs after الذين indicate renewed and enduring covenant-breaking, severing, and corruption, intensifying blame.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r3.anchor: وفي وصل الذين بالمضارع وعطف المضارعين عليه دليل على تجدد النقض والقطع والإفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r4.claim: The passive يوصل is more inclusive than an active form because it includes what the wrongdoers or someone else was commanded to join.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r4.anchor: وبناء يوصل للمفعول هو أبلغ من بنائه للفاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r5.claim: The order moves from the specific act of covenant-breaking, to the broader severing of commanded ties, to the still broader category of corruption; all are fruits of sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r5.anchor: قد بدأ أولا بنقض العهد، وهو أخص هذه الثلاث، ثم ثنى بقطع ما أمر الله بوصله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r6.claim: The active participle in الفاسقين marks a settled trait, while its consequences recur; combining fixed root and renewed branches makes the blame stronger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r6.anchor: وأتى باسم الفاعل صلة للألف واللام ليدل على ثبوتهم في هذه الصفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r7.claim: أولئك points to the people gathered by those blameworthy traits, and الخاسرون means those whose share and honor are diminished or who are destroyed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r7.anchor: أولئك، أي: أولئك الجامعون لتلك الأوصاف الذميمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r8.claim: Loss is explained as trading loyalty for breach, connection for severance, reform for corruption, and reward for punishment; other readings say they lose Paradise's bliss or forfeit good deeds through unbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r8.anchor: وسبب خسرانهم استبدالهم النقض بالوفاء، والقطع بالوصل، والإفساد بالإصلاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r9.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r9.claim: Al-Qaffāl says خاسر is a general name for anyone whose deed earns a recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r9.anchor: قال القفال: الخاسر اسم عام يقع على كل من عمل عملا يجزى عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r10.claim: The verse applies to Jews, with their scriptural deeds, and hypocrites, who outwardly act like sincere believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r10.anchor: والآية في اليهود، ولهم أعمال في شريعتهم وفي المنافقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r4.claim: Parables guide believers and mislead those who reject them; the passage condemns covenant-breakers who sever what must be joined and corrupt the earth, warning that this causes loss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r4.anchor: وأن في ضربه هدى لمن آمن، وضلالا لمن صد عنه، وذم من نقض عهد الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.claim: The relative clause may be accusative by syntactic attachment or by detachment for condemnation, or nominative as a new subject whose predicate is 'those are the losers'; this last reading makes the statement nearly parenthetical.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.anchor: يحتمل النصب والرفع والأول إما على الإتباع أو القطع أي أذم والثاني إما على الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the covenant metaphor by the conventional image of a cord, representing the stable connection between two parties.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.anchor: كما قال الزمخشري من حيث تسميتهم العهد بالحبل على سبيل الإستعارة لما فيه من ثبات الوصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.claim: Al-Alusi analyzes naqd as a vivid explicit metaphor for undoing an organized body, made apt by the implicit comparison of the covenant to a cord; this shows implicit metaphor can occur without an imagined image.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.anchor: والحاصل أن في الآية استعارة بالكناية والنقض استعارة تحقيقية تصريحية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.claim: One interpretation makes the covenant the rational evidence God established through human nature, the cosmos, prophets, and scripture; on this reading its breakers are all unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.anchor: إما العهد المأخوذ بالعقل وهو الحجة القائمة على عباده تعالى الدالة على وجوده ووحدته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation is the pledge conveyed by messengers: when a messenger comes with miracles they must affirm and follow him, as earlier scriptures mention; breakers are then the People of the Book and their hypocrites.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.anchor: وأما المأخوذ من جهة الرسل على الأمم بأنهم إذا بعث إليهم رسول مصدق بالمعجزات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.claim: Other reported meanings are the trust borne by humanity after the heavens and earth declined it, or Israel's pledges not to shed blood or expel one another; these reflect different proposed occasions of revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.anchor: وقيل الأمانة التي حملها الإنسان بعد إباء السموات والأرض عن أن يحملنها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the general meaning of God's covenant because the wording gives no decisive basis for restricting it; views about its particular referents rest on differing revelation-context reports.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.claim: Min is primarily spatial or temporal departure after the covenant was confirmed, implying they broke it immediately after securing it; treating it as an empty connective is remote. Mīthāq is what confirmed the covenant, a source according to some and a noun according to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.anchor: وتدل على أن النقض حصل عقيب توثق العهد من غير فصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows mīthāq to be a verbal noun meaning confirmation; its pronoun may refer to God's covenant or to the covenant itself, making the source annexed to agent or object respectively.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r1.anchor: وأفهم كلام أبي البقاء أن الميثاق هنا مصدر بمعنى التوثقة وفي الضمير الإحتمالان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r2.speaker: الساليكوتي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r2.claim: Al-Sālikūtī rejects taking the pronoun in 'its confirmation' back to God, since the meaning depends on reference to the covenant and a return to a possessed noun is disfavored; al-Alusi notes that such reference is common in verbal genitives.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r2.anchor: ولم يجوزه الساليكوتي لأن المعنى لا يتم بدون اعتبار العهد فهو أهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains what they sever as the Messenger, whom they cut off through denial and disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r3.anchor: الأول رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قطعوه بالتكذيب والعصيان قاله الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r4.claim: Other interpretations of what God commanded to be joined are the revealed word left unpracticed, affirmation of all prophets rather than some, or kinship ties; Qatāda gives the kinship interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r4.anchor: الثاني القول فإنه تعالى أمر أن يوصل بالعمل فلم يصلوه ولم يعملوا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r5.claim: Al-Alusi prefers a comprehensive reading: whatever causes the intended bond between God and servant is covered, giving the phrase its full general scope without unsupported restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r5.anchor: الخامس الأمر الشامل لما ذكر مما يوجب قطعه قطع الوصلة بين الله تعالى وبين العبد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r6.claim: Some prefer kinship ties because they see the verse progressing from violation of God's right to violation of people's rights; al-Alusi finds this argument weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r6.anchor: ورجح بعضهم ما قبله بأن الظاهر أن هذا توصيف للفاسقين بأنهم يضيعون حق الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r7.claim: The Muʿtazilites define a command as a verbal request for an act issued from a position of superiority; Abū al-Ḥusayn instead says the speaker must claim superiority, a definition challenged by Pharaoh's quoted request.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r7.anchor: والأمر القول الطالب للفعل مع علو عند المعتزلة أو استعلاء عند أبي الحسين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r8.speaker: الفقهاء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r8.claim: Jurists treat amr as shared between speech and action, citing the description of Pharaoh's command as not rightly guided.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r8.anchor: وذهب الفقهاء إلى أن الأمر مشترك بين القول والفعل لأنه يطلق عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r9.claim: The clause 'that it be joined' is best taken as a genitive or accusative apposition to the pronoun in 'what God commanded,' because that makes severing what was ordered joined more forceful; other parsing proposals are rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r9.anchor: يحتمل النصب والخفض على أنه بدل من

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r10.claim: Their corruption includes committing sins whose harm spreads, which is preferable to narrower readings of recruiting others into unbelief or intimidating routes to block migration; 'on earth' emphasizes harm beyond themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r10.anchor: أو بأنهم يرتكبون كل معصية يتعدى ضررها ويطير في الآفاق شررها ولعل هذا أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r11.claim: The demonstrative refers to the fāsiqūn through their detailed traits and signals their great distance in blame; exclusive 'losers' describes their complete loss of reason, eternal life, reward, capital, and profit, extending the preceding trade metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p211/r11.anchor: حصر الخاسرين عليهم باعتبار كمالهم في الخسران

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r1.claim: Naqḍ means breaking; the verse's people violate or abandon God's covenant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r1.anchor: فقال {الذين ينقضون} يخالفون ويتركون وأصل النقض الكسر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r2.claim: The covenant may be the primordial pledge that God is their Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r2.anchor: {عهد الله} أمر الله الذي عهد إليهم يوم الميثاق بقوله: "ألست بربكم قالوا بلى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r3.claim: Another view identifies it as the covenant taken from prophets and other communities to believe in Muhammad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r3.anchor: وقيل: أراد به العهد الذي أخذه على النبيين وسائر الأمم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r4.claim: Another view takes it as the Torah's covenant to believe in Muhammad and make his description known.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد به العهد الذي عهد إليهم في التوراة أن يؤمنوا بمحمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r5.claim: After its covenant means after its confirmation; mithāq is a firmly confirmed covenant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r5.anchor: من بعد ميثاقه} توكيده. والميثاق: العهد المؤكد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r6.claim: Severing what God ordered joined means rejecting Muhammad and some messengers while accepting others, contrary to believers' refusal to distinguish among messengers; another view means severing kinship ties.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r6.anchor: يعني الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وبجميع الرسل عليهم السلام لأنهم قالوا: نؤمن ببعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r7.claim: Their corruption consists of sins and obstructing people from believing in Muhammad and the Qur'an; losers are those cheated of their due. The following address turns in astonishment to Arab polytheists.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77/r7.anchor: {ويفسدون في الأرض} بالمعاصي وتعويق الناس عن الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وبالقرآن {أولئك هم الخاسرون} المغبونون

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r1.claim: The phrase about covenant-breakers modifies the transgressors, condemning and confirming their transgression.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r2.claim: Naqḍ literally loosens a rope's strands; breaking a covenant extends the rope image because a covenant binds the two parties.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r2.anchor: والنقض: فسخ التركيب، وأصله في طاقات الحبل، واستعماله في إبطال العهد من حيث إن العهد يستعار له الحبل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r3.claim: A covenant may be a binding charge or anything maintained and revisited; here it may be rational evidence for God's unity, existence, and messenger, linked to the primordial testimony.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r3.anchor: وهذا العهد: إما العهد المأخوذ بالعقل، وهو الحجة القائمة على عباده الدالة على توحيده ووجوب وجوده وصدق رسوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r4.claim: Alternatively, the covenant was taken through messengers from their communities: believe and follow an authenticated messenger without concealing or opposing his ruling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r4.anchor: أو: المأخوذ بالرسل على الأمم، بأنهم إذا بعث إليهم رسول مصدق بالمعجزات صدقوه واتبعوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r5.claim: An unnamed view divides God's covenants into one with Adam's descendants to affirm lordship, one with prophets to uphold religion without division, and one with scholars to disclose truth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27/r5.anchor: وقيل: عهود الله تعالى ثلاثة: عهد أخذه على جميع ذرية آدم بأن يقروا بربوبيته

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.claim: Mīthāq names what makes the covenant firm: God's signs and books, the people's undertaking and acceptance, or the verbal act itself; min marks the start of breaking after confirmation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r1.anchor: والميثاق: اسم لما يقع به الوثاقة وهي الاستحكام، والمراد به ما وثق الله به عهده من الآيات والكتب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.claim: The severed bonds may include kinship, alliance with believers, unity in affirming prophets and books, obligatory congregational prayer, any abandoned good, or evil that cuts the intended bond between God and servant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r2.anchor: يحتمل كل قطيعة لا يرضاها الله تعالى، كقطع الرحم، والإعراض عن موالاة المؤمنين، والتفرقة بين الأنبياء عليهم السلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.claim: Amr is a verbal request for action, perhaps with superiority or authority; affairs are named from what is commanded, while shaʾn is tied to requesting or intending a purpose.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r3.anchor: والأمر هو للقول الطالب للفعل، وقيل: مع العلو، وقيل: مع الاستعلاء، وبه سمي الأمر الذي هو واحد الأمور تسمية للمفعول به بالمصدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.claim: An tuṣal may be accusative or genitive as an appositive to mā or its pronoun; the latter is better in wording and meaning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#2/r4.anchor: يحتمل النصب والخفض على أنه بدل من ما، أو ضميره. والثاني أحسن لفظا ومعنى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r1.claim: They spread corruption by blocking faith, mocking truth, and severing the ties that order and sustain the world.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r1.anchor: بالمنع عن الإيمان والاستهزاء بالحق، وقطع الوصل التي بها نظام العالم وصلاحه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r2.claim: Their losses come from neglecting reason and eternal life, replacing belief and contemplation with denial and attack, fidelity with breach, reform with corruption, and reward with punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:27#3/r2.anchor: الذين خسروا بإهمال العقل عن النظر واقتناص ما يفيدهم الحياة الأبدية، واستبدال الإنكار والطعن في الآيات بالإيمان بها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r7.claim: The covenant is the commitment grounded in human reason and the signs God set up; its particular form is the sending of messengers, with scriptures confirming and easing reflection on it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r7.anchor: بما ركز فيهم من العقول ونصب لهم من الدلائل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r8.claim: A mīthāq is a firm bond; here the prophets' books confirm the covenant already brought close to human nature and made easy for reflection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r8.anchor: بدلالة الكتب على ألسنة الرسل مع تقريبه من الفطر وتسهيله للنظر , والوثاق شدة الربط

BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r9.claim: Cutting what God commands to join means severing connected innate dispositions and other goods; God commands their completion with further knowledge so they reach their fullest development.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p76/r9.anchor: القطع الإبانة في الشيء الواحد والوصل مصيرا لتكملة مع المكمل شيئا واحدا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r1.claim: Corruption on earth consists of putting an inferior opposite in place of what should be complete and leaving incomplete what should be perfected; the earth is where bodily and moral forms grow.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r1.anchor: { وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها ويهلك الحرث والنسل والله لا يحب الفساد }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r2.claim: The losers diminish what should grow: across their three linked conditions they reduce their own capital, and the distant demonstrative places them far from good.

DURR-FULL:v1p103/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p103/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p103/r1.claim: When polytheists objected to Qur'anic references to flies and the spider's house, God revealed the parable verse; the report cites the fly's inability to recover what idols take and the spider's web.
DURR-FULL:v1p103/r1.anchor: عن الن عباس قال: إن الله ذكر آلهة المشركين فقال (وإن يسلبهم الذباب شيئا) وذكر كيد الآلهة كبيت العنكبوت

DURR-FULL:v1p104/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r2.claim: Saʿd warns against breaking the covenant and identifies the Kharijites as those who break God's covenant after its solemn pledge; he called them wicked.
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: الحرورية هم {الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه} قال: إياكم ونقض هذا الميثاق

DURR-FULL:v1p104/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r3.claim: Qatada says God hates and severely threatens covenant-breaking; anyone who gives God a heartfelt pledge must fulfill it, and he knows no sin threatened so strongly.
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه} قال: إياكم ونقض هذا الميثاق

DURR-FULL:v1p104/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r4.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r4.claim: The Prophet says a person without trustworthiness has no faith and a person without a covenant has no religion.
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r4.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال ألا لا إيمان لمن لا أمانة له ولا دين لمن لا عهد له

DURR-FULL:v1p104/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r5.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت وأبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r5.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits the same saying from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit and Abu Umama.
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r5.anchor:
عبادة بن الصامت وأبي أمامة
مثله

DURR-FULL:v1p104/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r6.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits the same saying from Ibn ʿUmar.
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r6.anchor:
من حديث ابن عمر
مثله
وأخرج البخاري في تاريخه والحاكم

DURR-FULL:v1p104/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r7.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r7.claim: The Prophet says good keeping of a covenant is part of faith.
